title.zh: 卷八十五 志第六十一 河渠三
title.raw: 卷八十五 志第六十一 河渠三 Volume 85 Treatises 61: Rivers and Canals 3

sentences.zh: 運河上

translations.literal: On the Canal Transport Route
translations.idiomatic: Canal Transport

sentences.zh: 明成祖肇建北京，轉漕東南，水陸兼輓，仍元人之舊，參用海運。

translations.literal: When Emperor Chengzu of Ming first established Beijing, he diverted grain transport from the southeast, employing both land and water haulage, following the Yuan practice while also making partial use of sea transport.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongle Emperor first established Beijing, he redirected grain tribute from the southeast, relying on both land and water haulage in the Yuan manner while supplementing the system with sea transport.

sentences.zh: 逮會通河開，海陸並罷。

translations.literal: Once the Huitong Canal was opened, both sea and land routes were abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: After the Huitong Canal was opened, both the sea route and the land haul were discontinued.

sentences.zh: 南極江口，北盡大通橋，運道三千餘里。

translations.literal: Its southern terminus reached the river mouth; its northern limit was Datong Bridge—the transport route extended over three thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: From the river mouth in the south to Datong Bridge in the north, the transport route ran more than three thousand li.

sentences.zh: 綜而計之，自昌平神山泉諸水，匯貫都城，過大通橋，東至通州入白河者，大通河也。

translations.literal: Taking it all together, the waters from Shenshan Spring in Changping and other sources, converging and flowing through the capital, passing Datong Bridge, and eastward to Tongzhou where they enter the Bai River—this is the Datong River.
translations.idiomatic: Taken as a whole, the Datong River consists of the waters from Shenshan Spring in Changping and other sources that converge and flow through the capital, pass Datong Bridge, and run east to Tongzhou, where they enter the Bai River.

sentences.zh: 自通州而南至直沽，會衛河入海者，白河也。

translations.literal: From Tongzhou southward to Zhigu, where it joins the Wei River and enters the sea—this is the Bai River.
translations.idiomatic: The Bai River runs from Tongzhou south to Zhigu, where it meets the Wei River and flows into the sea.

sentences.zh: 自臨清而北至直沽，會白河入海者，衛水也。

translations.literal: From Linqing northward to Zhigu, where it joins the Bai River and enters the sea—this is the Wei River.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei River runs from Linqing north to Zhigu, where it meets the Bai River and enters the sea.

sentences.zh: 自汶上南旺分流，北經張秋至臨清，會衛河，南至濟寧天井閘，會泗、沂、洸三水者，汶水也。

translations.literal: From the Nanwang diversion in Wenshang, northward through Zhangqiu to Linqing where it joins the Wei River, and southward to the Tianjing Sluice at Jining where it meets the Si, Yi, and Guang Rivers—this is the Wen River.
translations.idiomatic: The Wen River divides at Nanwang in Wenshang: its northern branch runs through Zhangqiu to Linqing and joins the Wei River, while its southern branch reaches the Tianjing Sluice at Jining, where it meets the Si, Yi, and Guang Rivers.

sentences.zh: 自濟寧出天井閘，與汶合流，至南陽新河，舊出茶城，會黃、沁後出夏鎮，循泇河達直口，入黃濟運者，泗、洸、小沂河及山東泉水也。

translations.literal: From Jining exiting the Tianjing Sluice, joining the Wen River, reaching the Nanyang New Canal—formerly exiting at Chacheng, meeting the Huang and Qin Rivers, later exiting at Xiazhen, following the Jia River to Zhikou, and entering the Yellow River to aid transport—these are the Si, Guang, and Lesser Yi Rivers and the springs of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: From Jining the Tianjing Sluice releases water that joins the Wen River and flows to the Nanyang New Canal; formerly it exited at Chacheng and met the Huang and Qin Rivers, later it exited at Xiazhen and followed the Jia River to Zhikou, where it entered the Yellow River to support transport—these waters are the Si, Guang, and Lesser Yi Rivers together with the springs of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 自茶城秦溝，南曆徐、呂，浮邳，會大沂河，至清河縣入淮後，從直河口抵清口者，黃河水也。

translations.literal: From Chacheng and Qin Ditch, southward through Xu and Lü, floating past Pi, joining the Great Yi River, entering the Huai at Qinghe County, then from Zhihekou reaching Qingkou—this is the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River runs from Chacheng and Qin Ditch south through Xu and Lü, past Pi, where it joins the Great Yi River; after entering the Huai at Qinghe County, it reaches Qingkou from Zhihekou.

sentences.zh: 自清口而南，至於瓜、儀者，淮、揚諸湖水也。

translations.literal: From Qingkou southward to Guazhou and Yizhen—these are the lakes of Huai and Yang.
translations.idiomatic: From Qingkou south to Guazhou and Yizhen, the route passes through the lakes of the Huai and Yang regions.

sentences.zh: 過此則長江矣。

translations.literal: Beyond this lies the Yangtze River.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond this point lies the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 長江以南，則松、蘇、浙江運道也。

translations.literal: South of the Yangtze are the transport routes of Songjiang, Suzhou, and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Yangtze lie the transport routes of Songjiang, Suzhou, and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 淮、揚至京口以南之河，通謂之轉運河，而由瓜、儀達淮安者，又謂之南河，由黃河達豐、沛曰中河，由山東達天津曰北河，由天津達張家灣曰通濟河，而總名曰漕河。

translations.literal: The rivers from Huai and Yang to south of Jingkou are generally called the Transport Canal; that from Guazhou and Yizhen reaching Huai'an is also called the Southern River; that from the Yellow River reaching Feng and Pei is called the Central River; that from Shandong reaching Tianjin is called the Northern River; that from Tianjin reaching Zhangjiawan is called the Tongji River—and collectively they are called the Tribute Canal.
translations.idiomatic: The waterways from the Huai and Yang regions south to Jingkou are collectively known as the Transport Canal. The section from Guazhou and Yizhen to Huai'an is called the Southern River; that from the Yellow River to Feng and Pei is the Central River; that from Shandong to Tianjin is the Northern River; and that from Tianjin to Zhangjiawan is the Tongji River. All together they are known as the Tribute Canal.

sentences.zh: 其逾京師而東若薊州，西北若昌平，皆嘗有河通，轉漕餉軍。

translations.literal: Beyond the capital to the east such as Jizhou, and to the northwest such as Changping, canals had at various times been opened to transport grain and supply the armies.
translations.idiomatic: East of the capital at places such as Jizhou, and northwest at places such as Changping, canals had at times been opened to move grain tribute and supply the troops.

sentences.zh: 漕河之別，曰白漕、衛漕、閘漕、河漕、湖漕、江漕、浙漕。

translations.literal: The divisions of the Tribute Canal are: Bai Canal, Wei Canal, Sluice Canal, River Canal, Lake Canal, Yangtze Canal, and Zhejiang Canal.
translations.idiomatic: The Tribute Canal is divided into seven sections: the Bai, Wei, Sluice, River, Lake, Yangtze, and Zhejiang Canals.

sentences.zh: 因地為號，流俗所通稱也。

translations.literal: They are named according to locality—common popular designations.
translations.idiomatic: These names derive from local geography and reflect common usage.

sentences.zh: 淮、揚諸水所匯，徐、兗河流所經，疏瀹決排，繄人力是系，故閘、河、湖於轉漕尤急。

translations.literal: Where the waters of Huai and Yang converge, and where the rivers of Xu and Yan pass—all dredging, clearing, and drainage depend on human labor; therefore the sluice, river, and lake sections are especially critical for transport.
translations.idiomatic: Where the waters of Huai and Yang converge and the rivers of Xu and Yan flow, dredging, clearing, and drainage all depend on human effort; for this reason the sluice, river, and lake sections of the transport route are especially urgent concerns.

sentences.zh: 閘漕者，即會通河。

translations.literal: Sluice Canal transport is the Huitong Canal.
translations.idiomatic: The Sluice Canal section is the Huitong Canal.

sentences.zh: 北至臨清，與衛河會，南出茶城口，與黃河會，資汶、洸、泗水及山東泉源。

translations.literal: Northward to Linqing where it joins the Wei River; southward exiting Chacheng Mouth to join the Yellow River; it draws on the Wen, Guang, and Si Rivers and the springs of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: It runs north to Linqing, where it meets the Wei River, and south through Chacheng Mouth to join the Yellow River, drawing on the Wen, Guang, and Si Rivers and the springs of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 泉源之派有五。

translations.literal: The spring sources divide into five branches.
translations.idiomatic: The spring sources fall into five branches.

sentences.zh: 曰分水者，汶水派也，泉百四十有五。

translations.literal: That called Fenshui is the branch of the Wen River, with one hundred forty-five springs.
translations.idiomatic: The Fenshui branch belongs to the Wen River system and comprises one hundred forty-five springs.

sentences.zh: 曰天井者，濟河派也，泉九十有六。

translations.literal: That called Tianjing is the branch of the Ji River, with ninety-six springs.
translations.idiomatic: The Tianjing branch belongs to the Ji River system and comprises ninety-six springs.

sentences.zh: 曰魯橋者，泗河派也，泉二十有六。

translations.literal: That called Luqiao is the branch of the Si River, with twenty-six springs.
translations.idiomatic: The Luqiao branch belongs to the Si River system and comprises twenty-six springs.

sentences.zh: 曰沙河者，新河派也，二十有八。

translations.literal: That called Shahe is the branch of the New Canal, with twenty-eight springs.
translations.idiomatic: The Shahe branch belongs to the New Canal system and comprises twenty-eight springs.

sentences.zh: 曰邳州者，沂河派也，泉十有六。

translations.literal: That called Pizhou is the branch of the Yi River, with sixteen springs.
translations.idiomatic: The Pizhou branch belongs to the Yi River system and comprises sixteen springs.

sentences.zh: 諸泉所匯為湖，其浸十五。

translations.literal: The lakes into which the springs converge number fifteen.
translations.idiomatic: The springs converge to form lakes, of which there are fifteen.

sentences.zh: 曰南旺，東西二湖，周百五十餘里，運渠貫其中。

translations.literal: That called Nanwang consists of eastern and western lakes, with a circumference of over one hundred fifty li, through which the transport channel runs.
translations.idiomatic: Nanwang comprises eastern and western lakes with a combined circumference of more than one hundred fifty li; the transport channel runs through them.

sentences.zh: 北曰馬蹋，南曰蜀山，曰蘇魯。

translations.literal: To the north is Mata; to the south are Shushan and Sulu.
translations.idiomatic: To the north is Mata; to the south are Shushan and Sulu.

sentences.zh: 又南曰馬場。

translations.literal: Further south is Machang.
translations.idiomatic: Farther south is Machang.

sentences.zh: 又南八十里曰南陽，亦曰獨山，周七十餘里。

translations.literal: Eighty li further south is Nanyang, also called Dushan, with a circumference of over seventy li.
translations.idiomatic: Eighty li farther south lies Nanyang, also known as Dushan, with a circumference of more than seventy li.

sentences.zh: 北曰安山，周八十三里。

translations.literal: To the north is Anshan, with a circumference of eighty-three li.
translations.idiomatic: To the north is Anshan, with a circumference of eighty-three li.

sentences.zh: 南曰大、小昭陽，大湖袤十八里，小湖殺三之一，周八十餘里。

translations.literal: To the south are Greater and Lesser Zhaoyang; the greater lake extends eighteen li, the lesser lake is one-third smaller, with a combined circumference of over eighty li.
translations.idiomatic: To the south are the Greater and Lesser Zhaoyang lakes; the greater lake spans eighteen li, the lesser is one-third smaller, and together they have a circumference of more than eighty li.

sentences.zh: 由馬家橋留城閘而南，曰武家，曰赤山，曰微山，曰呂孟，曰張王諸湖，連注八十里，引薛河由地浜溝出，會於赤龍潭，並趨茶城。

translations.literal: From Majia Bridge and Liucheng Sluice southward are the lakes of Wujia, Chishan, Weishan, Lümeng, and Zhangwang, connected for eighty li; the Xue River is diverted through Dibin Ditch, converging at Chilongtan, and all flow together toward Chacheng.
translations.idiomatic: South from Majia Bridge and Liucheng Sluice lie the lakes of Wujia, Chishan, Weishan, Lümeng, and Zhangwang, linked in a chain eighty li long; the Xue River is channeled out through Dibin Ditch, meets at Chilongtan, and all waters flow together toward Chacheng.

sentences.zh: 自南旺分水北至臨清三百里，地降九十尺，為閘二十有一；

translations.literal: From the Nanwang diversion north to Linqing is three hundred li, with a drop of ninety chi, and twenty-one sluices were built;
translations.idiomatic: From the Nanwang diversion north to Linqing is three hundred li, with a drop of ninety chi and twenty-one sluices;

sentences.zh: 南至鎮口三百九十里，地降百十有六尺，為閘二十有七。

translations.literal: South to Zhenkou is three hundred ninety li, with a drop of one hundred sixteen chi, and twenty-seven sluices were built.
translations.idiomatic: South to Zhenkou is three hundred ninety li, with a drop of one hundred sixteen chi and twenty-seven sluices.

sentences.zh: 其外又有積水、進水、減水、平水之閘五十有四。

translations.literal: Beyond these there were additionally fifty-four sluices for storing water, admitting water, releasing water, and leveling water.
translations.idiomatic: In addition there were fifty-four sluices for storing, admitting, releasing, and leveling water.

sentences.zh: 又為壩二十有一，所以防運河之泄，佐閘以為用者也。

translations.literal: There were also twenty-one dams, serving to prevent the transport canal from draining away and to assist the sluices in their function.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-one dams were also built to prevent the transport canal from losing water and to assist the sluices in their operation.

sentences.zh: 其後開泇河二百六十里，為閘十一，為壩四。

translations.literal: Later the Si River Canal of two hundred sixty li was opened, with eleven sluices and four dams.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Si River Canal was opened for two hundred sixty li, with eleven sluices and four dams.

sentences.zh: 運舟不出鎮口，與黃河會於董溝。

translations.literal: Transport vessels no longer exited at Zhenkou but joined the Yellow River at Donggou.
translations.idiomatic: Transport vessels no longer passed through Zhenkou but instead joined the Yellow River at Donggou.

sentences.zh: 河漕者，即黃河。

translations.literal: River Canal transport is the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: The River Canal section is the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 上自茶城與會通河會，下至清口與淮河會。

translations.literal: Above, from Chacheng where it joins the Huitong Canal; below, to Qingkou where it joins the Huai River.
translations.idiomatic: It runs from Chacheng, where it meets the Huitong Canal, down to Qingkou, where it meets the Huai River.

sentences.zh: 其道有三：中路曰濁河，北路曰銀河，南路曰符離河。

translations.literal: Its route has three branches: the central route is called the Zhuo River, the northern route the Yin River, and the southern route the Fuli River.
translations.idiomatic: The route has three branches: the central route is the Zhuo River, the northern route is the Yin River, and the southern route is the Fuli River.

sentences.zh: 南近陵，北近運，惟中路去陵遠，於運有濟。

translations.literal: The southern route lies near the imperial tombs, the northern route near the transport route; only the central route is far from the tombs and beneficial to transport.
translations.idiomatic: The southern route runs close to the imperial tombs and the northern route close to the transport route; only the central route, being far from the tombs, serves transport effectively.

sentences.zh: 而河流遷徙不常，上流苦潰，下流苦淤。

translations.literal: Yet the river's course shifted constantly; the upper reaches suffered from breaches, the lower reaches from silting.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the river shifted its course unpredictably—the upper reaches were plagued by breaches, the lower reaches by silting.

sentences.zh: 運道自南而北，出清口，經桃、宿，溯二洪，入鎮口，陟險五百餘里。

translations.literal: The transport route from south to north exited Qingkou, passed through Tao and Su, ascended the Two Hongs, entered Zhenkou—a hazardous journey of over five hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: The transport route ran south to north from Qingkou through Tao and Su, up the Two Hongs, and into Zhenkou—a treacherous passage of more than five hundred li.

sentences.zh: 自二洪以上，河與漕不相涉也。

translations.literal: Above the Two Hongs, the river and the transport route did not intersect.
translations.idiomatic: Above the Two Hongs, the river and the transport route did not intersect.

sentences.zh: 至泇河開而二洪避，董溝闢而直河淤，運道之資河者二百六十里而止，董溝以上，河又無病於漕也。

translations.literal: When the Si River Canal was opened the Two Hongs were bypassed; when Donggou was opened the direct river route silted up; the transport route's reliance on the river extended only two hundred sixty li, and above Donggou the river no longer harmed transport.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Si River Canal was opened, the Two Hongs were bypassed; once Donggou was opened, the direct river route silted up. The transport route relied on the river for only two hundred sixty li, and above Donggou the river no longer threatened transport.

sentences.zh: 湖漕者，由淮安抵揚州三百七十里，地卑積水，匯為澤國。

translations.literal: Lake Canal transport runs from Huai'an to Yangzhou for three hundred seventy li; the low-lying terrain accumulates water, forming a marshland country.
translations.idiomatic: The Lake Canal section runs three hundred seventy li from Huai'an to Yangzhou; the low-lying terrain holds water and forms a vast marshland.

sentences.zh: 山陽則有管家、射陽，寶應則有白馬、汜光，高郵則有石臼、甓社、武安、邵伯諸湖。

translations.literal: In Shanyang there are Guanjia and Sheyang; in Baoying there are Baima and Siguang; in Gaoyou there are the lakes of Shijiu, Bishe, Wu'an, and Shaobo.
translations.idiomatic: Shanyang has the Guanjia and Sheyang lakes; Baoying has Baima and Siguang; Gaoyou has the lakes of Shijiu, Bishe, Wu'an, and Shaobo.

sentences.zh: 仰受上流之水，傍接諸山之源，巨浸連亙，由五塘以達於江。

translations.literal: They receive water from upstream and connect with the sources of various mountains; vast expanses of water stretch continuously, reaching the river through the Five Dikes.
translations.idiomatic: They receive upstream waters and connect with mountain sources; vast stretches of water extend in succession, reaching the river through the Five Dikes.

sentences.zh: 慮淮東侵，築高家堰拒其上流，築王簡、張福二堤禦其分泄。

translations.literal: Fearing eastern encroachment by the Huai, the Gaojia Dam was built to block its upper flow, and the Wangjian and Zhangfu dikes were built to guard against its diversion.
translations.idiomatic: To guard against the Huai River encroaching from the east, the Gaojia Dam was built to hold back its upper waters, and the Wangjian and Zhangfu dikes were built to prevent its diversion.

sentences.zh: 慮淮侵而漕敗，開淮安永濟、高郵康濟、寶應弘濟三月河以通舟。

translations.literal: Fearing that Huai encroachment would ruin transport, the Sanyue Canals of Yongji at Huai'an, Kangji at Gaoyou, and Hongji at Baoying were opened to allow passage of vessels.
translations.idiomatic: To prevent Huai encroachment from disrupting transport, the Sanyue Canals—Yongji at Huai'an, Kangji at Gaoyou, and Hongji at Baoying—were opened to allow vessels to pass.

sentences.zh: 至揚子灣東，則分二道：一由儀真通江口，以漕上江湖廣、江西；

translations.literal: At Yangzi Bay to the east, the route divided into two: one from Yizhen through the river mouth to transport grain upstream to Huguang and Jiangxi;
translations.idiomatic: East of Yangzi Bay the route divided in two: one branch ran from Yizhen through the river mouth to transport grain upstream to Huguang and Jiangxi;

sentences.zh: 一由瓜洲通西江嘴，以漕下江兩浙。

translations.literal: One from Guazhou through Xijiangzui to transport grain downstream to the two Zhe provinces.
translations.idiomatic: the other ran from Guazhou through Xijiangzui to transport grain downstream to the two Zhe provinces.

sentences.zh: 本非河道，專取諸湖之水，故曰湖漕。

translations.literal: These were originally not river routes but relied solely on lake waters; hence they are called Lake Canal transport.
translations.idiomatic: These were not originally river routes but drew exclusively on lake waters; hence the name Lake Canal.

sentences.zh: 太祖初起大軍北伐，開蹋場口、耐牢坡，通漕以餉梁、晉。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor first raised his great army for the northern expedition, he opened Tacangkou and Nailaopo to open transport and supply Liang and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hongwu Emperor first raised his great army for the northern expedition, he opened Tacangkou and Nailaopo to establish transport and supply the regions of Liang and Jin.

sentences.zh: 定都應天，運道通利：江西、湖廣之粟，浮江直下；

translations.literal: After establishing the capital at Yingtian, the transport routes were convenient: grain from Jiangxi and Huguang floated down the river directly;
translations.idiomatic: After establishing the capital at Yingtian, the transport routes functioned smoothly: grain from Jiangxi and Huguang floated directly downriver;

sentences.zh: 浙西、吳中之粟，由轉運河；

translations.literal: Grain from western Zhe and Wuzhong went by the Transport Canal;
translations.idiomatic: grain from western Zhe and Wuzhong traveled by the Transport Canal;

sentences.zh: 鳳、泗之粟，浮淮；

translations.literal: Grain from Feng and Si floated on the Huai;
translations.idiomatic: grain from Feng and Si traveled on the Huai;

sentences.zh: 河南、山東之粟，下黃河。

translations.literal: Grain from Henan and Shandong went down the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: and grain from Henan and Shandong went down the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 嘗由開封運粟，溯河達渭，以給陝西，用海運以餉遼卒，有事於西北者甚鮮。

translations.literal: Grain was once transported from Kaifeng, going upstream on the river to reach the Wei to supply Shaanxi; sea transport was used to supply Liaodong troops—matters concerning the northwest were very few.
translations.idiomatic: Grain was at times shipped from Kaifeng, carried upstream to the Wei River to supply Shaanxi, while sea transport supplied the Liaodong garrisons; affairs concerning the northwest were relatively few.

sentences.zh: 淮、揚之間，築高郵湖堤二十餘里，開寶應倚湖直渠四十里，築堤護之。

translations.literal: Between Huai and Yang, the Gaoyou Lake dike of over twenty li was built, and a straight canal of forty li along the lake at Baoying was opened, with dikes built to protect it.
translations.idiomatic: Between the Huai and Yang regions, a dike more than twenty li long was built along Gaoyou Lake, and a straight canal forty li long was opened along the lake at Baoying, protected by accompanying dikes.

sentences.zh: 他小修築，無大利害也。

translations.literal: Other minor repairs had no great benefit or harm.
translations.idiomatic: Other minor repairs had little significant impact.

sentences.zh: 永樂四年，成祖命平江伯陳瑄督轉運，一仍由海，而一則浮淮入河，至陽武，陸挽百七十里抵衛輝，浮於衛，所謂陸海兼運者也。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongle, Chengzu ordered the Marquis of Pingjiang Chen Xuan to supervise transport: one route still went by sea, while another floated on the Huai into the river, reaching Yangwu, then overland haulage of one hundred seventy li to Weihui, then floating on the Wei—what was called combined land and sea transport.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 4, the Yongle Emperor appointed the Marquis of Pingjiang, Chen Xuan, to supervise transport: one route continued by sea, while another floated on the Huai into the river to Yangwu, then overland haulage for one hundred seventy li to Weihui, and finally on the Wei River—what was known as combined land and sea transport.

sentences.zh: 海運多險，陸挽亦艱。

translations.literal: Sea transport was full of dangers, and overland haulage was also arduous.
translations.idiomatic: Sea transport was perilous, and overland haulage was arduous as well.

sentences.zh: 九年二月乃用濟寧州同知潘叔正言，命尚書宋禮、侍郎金純、都督周長浚會通河。

translations.literal: In the second month of the ninth year, following the proposal of Pan Shuzheng, vice-prefect of Jining, Ministers Song Li and Jin Chun and Commander Zhou Chang were ordered to dredge the Huitong Canal.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Yongle 9, acting on the proposal of Pan Shuzheng, vice-prefect of Jining, the emperor ordered Ministers Song Li and Jin Chun and Commander Zhou Chang to dredge the Huitong Canal.

sentences.zh: 會通河者，元轉漕故道也，元末已廢不用。

translations.literal: The Huitong Canal was the old Yuan grain transport route, abandoned and unused by the end of the Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Huitong Canal was the old Yuan grain transport route, abandoned and unused by the end of the Yuan dynasty.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十四年，河決原武，漫安山湖而東，會通盡淤，至是復之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Hongwu, the river breached at Yuanwu, flooding eastward over Anshan Lake; the Huitong Canal was completely silted up, and now it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 24 the river breached at Yuanwu and flooded eastward over Anshan Lake, completely silting the Huitong Canal; now it was restored.

sentences.zh: 由濟寧至臨清三百八十五里，引汶、泗入其中。

translations.literal: From Jining to Linqing was three hundred eighty-five li, with the Wen and Si Rivers diverted into it.
translations.idiomatic: It ran three hundred eighty-five li from Jining to Linqing, with the Wen and Si Rivers diverted into it.

sentences.zh: 泗出泗水陪尾山，四泉併發，西流至兗州城東，合於沂。

translations.literal: The Si River emerges from Peiwei Mountain in Sishui; four springs burst forth together, flowing west to the east of Yanzhou city, where it joins the Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The Si River rises from Peiwei Mountain in Sishui, where four springs burst forth together; it flows west to the east of Yanzhou city and joins the Yi River.

sentences.zh: 汶河有二：小汶河出新泰宮山下；

translations.literal: The Wen River has two branches: the Lesser Wen River emerges from beneath Gong Mountain in Xintai;
translations.idiomatic: The Wen River has two branches: the Lesser Wen rises from beneath Gong Mountain in Xintai;

sentences.zh: 大汶河出泰安仙台嶺南，又出萊蕪原山陰及寨子村。

translations.literal: The Great Wen River emerges from the south of Xiantai Ridge in Tai'an, and also from the north of Yuan Mountain in Laiwu and from Zhaizi Village.
translations.idiomatic: the Great Wen rises from the south of Xiantai Ridge in Tai'an, and also from the north of Yuan Mountain in Laiwu and from Zhaizi Village.

sentences.zh: 俱至靜豐鎮合流，饒徂徠山陽，而小汶河來會。

translations.literal: Both reach Jingfeng Town and join, winding along the south of Mount Culai, where the Lesser Wen River comes to meet them.
translations.idiomatic: Both reach Jingfeng Town and merge, winding along the southern slope of Mount Culai, where the Lesser Wen joins them.

sentences.zh: 經甯陽北堈城，西南流百餘里，至汶上。

translations.literal: Passing Gangcheng in northern Ningyang, it flows southwest for over one hundred li to Wenshang.
translations.idiomatic: It passes Gangcheng in northern Ningyang and flows southwest for more than one hundred li to Wenshang.

sentences.zh: 其支流曰洸河，出堈城西南，流三十里，會甯陽諸泉，經濟寧東，與泗合。

translations.literal: Its tributary is called the Guang River, emerging from southwest of Gangcheng, flowing thirty li, meeting the springs of Ningyang, passing east of Jining, and joining the Si.
translations.idiomatic: Its tributary, the Guang River, rises southwest of Gangcheng, flows thirty li, meets the springs of Ningyang, passes east of Jining, and joins the Si River.

sentences.zh: 元初，畢輔國始於堈城左汶水陰作斗門，導汶入洸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuan, Bi Fuguo first built a sluice gate on the left bank beneath the Wen River at Gangcheng, diverting the Wen into the Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuan dynasty, Bi Fuguo first built a sluice gate on the left bank beneath the Wen River at Gangcheng to divert the Wen into the Guang.

sentences.zh: 至元中，又分流北入濟，由壽張至臨清，通漳、禦入海。

translations.literal: In the Zhiyuan era, it was further diverted north into the Ji River, from Shouzhang to Linqing, connecting with the Zhang and Yu Rivers to enter the sea.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhiyuan era it was further diverted north into the Ji River, from Shouzhang to Linqing, connecting with the Zhang and Yu Rivers to reach the sea.

sentences.zh: 南旺者，南北之脊也。

translations.literal: Nanwang is the watershed ridge between north and south.
translations.idiomatic: Nanwang is the watershed between north and south.

sentences.zh: 自左而南，距濟寧九十里，合沂、泗以濟；

translations.literal: From the left southward, ninety li from Jining, the Yi and Si Rivers join to supply it;
translations.idiomatic: To the south, ninety li from Jining, the Yi and Si Rivers join to supply it;

sentences.zh: 自右而北，距臨清三百餘里，無他水，獨賴汶。

translations.literal: From the right northward, over three hundred li from Linqing, there is no other water—it relies solely on the Wen.
translations.idiomatic: To the north, more than three hundred li from Linqing, there is no other water source—it relies entirely on the Wen River.

sentences.zh: 禮用汶上老人白英策，築壩東平之戴村，遏汶使無入洸，而盡出南旺，南北置閘三十八。

translations.literal: Song Li adopted the plan of the old man Bai Ying of Wenshang, building a dam at Daicun in Dongping to block the Wen from entering the Guang and channel all of it out at Nanwang, with thirty-eight sluices placed north and south.
translations.idiomatic: Song Li adopted the plan of Bai Ying, an old man of Wenshang, building a dam at Daicun in Dongping to block the Wen from entering the Guang and channel all its water out at Nanwang, with thirty-eight sluices placed north and south.

sentences.zh: 又開新河，自汶上袁家口左徙五十里至壽張之沙灣，以接舊河。

translations.literal: A new canal was also opened, diverting left from Yuanjiakou in Wenshang for fifty li to Shawan in Shouzhang, to connect with the old canal.
translations.idiomatic: A new canal was also opened, diverging left from Yuanjiakou in Wenshang for fifty li to Shawan in Shouzhang to connect with the old canal.

sentences.zh: 其秋，禮還，又請疏東平東境沙河淤沙三里，築堰障之，合馬常泊之流入會通濟運。

translations.literal: That autumn, when Song Li returned, he also requested dredging three li of silted sand on the Sha River in eastern Dongping, building a barrier dam, and joining the waters of Machang Lake into the Huitong to aid transport.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, upon Song Li's return, he also requested dredging three li of silted sand on the Sha River in eastern Dongping, building a barrier dam, and channeling the waters of Machang Lake into the Huitong Canal to support transport.

sentences.zh: 又於汶上、東平、濟寧、沛縣並湖地設水櫃、陡門。

translations.literal: Water cabinets and steep gates were also established at Wenshang, Dongping, Jining, Peixian, and lake areas.
translations.idiomatic: Water cabinets and steep gates were also installed at Wenshang, Dongping, Jining, Peixian, and the lake districts.

sentences.zh: 在漕河西者曰水櫃，東者曰陡門，櫃以蓄泉，門以泄漲。

translations.literal: Those on the west of the Tribute Canal are called water cabinets; those on the east are called steep gates—cabinets store spring water, gates release flood water.
translations.idiomatic: Those on the west side of the Tribute Canal are called water cabinets; those on the east are steep gates—cabinets store spring water, gates release floodwaters.

sentences.zh: 純復浚賈魯河故道，引黃水至塌場口會汶，經徐、呂入淮。

translations.literal: Jin Chun further dredged the old course of the Jia Lu River, diverting Yellow River water to Tacangkou to meet the Wen, passing through Xu and Lü to enter the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Chun further dredged the old course of the Jia Lu River, diverting Yellow River water to Tacangkou to meet the Wen River, passing through Xu and Lü to enter the Huai.

sentences.zh: 運道以定。

translations.literal: The transport route was thus established.
translations.idiomatic: The transport route was thus established.

sentences.zh: 其後宣宗時，嘗發軍民十二萬，浚濟寧以北自長溝至棗林閘百二十里，置閘諸淺，浚湖塘以引山泉。

translations.literal: Later, during the Xuande reign, one hundred twenty thousand soldiers and civilians were mobilized to dredge one hundred twenty li north of Jining from Changgou to Zaolin Sluice, building sluices at shallow sections and dredging lake ponds to draw in mountain springs.
translations.idiomatic: Later, during the Xuande reign, one hundred twenty thousand soldiers and civilians were mobilized to dredge one hundred twenty li north of Jining from Changgou to Zaolin Sluice, building sluices at shallow sections and dredging lake ponds to draw in mountain springs.

sentences.zh: 正統時，浚滕、沛淤河，又於濟寧、勝三州縣疏泉置閘，易金口堰土壩為石，蓄水以資會通。

translations.literal: During the Zhengtong reign, the silted rivers of Teng and Pei were dredged; springs were cleared and sluices built in Jining and the three prefectures and counties of Sheng; the earthen dam at Jinkou was replaced with stone to store water for the Huitong Canal.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengtong reign, the silted rivers of Teng and Pei were dredged; springs were cleared and sluices built in Jining and the three prefectures and counties of Sheng; the earthen dam at Jinkou was replaced with stone to store water for the Huitong Canal.

sentences.zh: 景帝時，增置濟寧抵臨清減水閘。

translations.literal: During the Jingtai reign, additional flood-release sluices were built from Jining to Linqing.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingtai reign, additional flood-release sluices were built from Jining to Linqing.

sentences.zh: 天順時，拓臨清舊閘，移五十丈。

translations.literal: During the Tianshun reign, the old sluice at Linqing was expanded, moved fifty zhang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianshun reign, the old sluice at Linqing was expanded and relocated fifty zhang.

sentences.zh: 憲宗時，築汶上、濟寧決堤百餘里，增南旺上、下及安山三閘。

translations.literal: During the Chenghua reign, breached dikes of over one hundred li at Wenshang and Jining were repaired, and three sluices were added at upper and lower Nanwang and Anshan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chenghua reign, breached dikes totaling more than one hundred li at Wenshang and Jining were repaired, and three sluices were added at upper Nanwang, lower Nanwang, and Anshan.

sentences.zh: 命工部侍郎杜謙勘治汶、泗、洸諸泉。

translations.literal: Vice-Minister of Works Du Qian was ordered to survey and manage the springs of the Wen, Si, and Guang Rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Vice-Minister of Works Du Qian was ordered to survey and manage the springs of the Wen, Si, and Guang Rivers.

sentences.zh: 武宗時，增置汶上袁家口及寺前鋪石閘，浚南旺淤八十里，而閘漕之治詳。

translations.literal: During the Wuzong reign, stone sluices were added at Yuanjiakou in Wenshang and Sidianpu; eighty li of silt at Nanwang was dredged, and the management of Sluice Canal transport was thoroughly detailed.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wuzong reign, stone sluices were added at Yuanjiakou in Wenshang and Sidianpu; eighty li of silt at Nanwang was dredged, and the management of the Sluice Canal section was thoroughly documented.

sentences.zh: 惟河決則挾漕而去，為大害。

translations.literal: Only when the river breached would it carry off the transport route—a great calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Only when the river breached would it sweep away the transport route—a grave disaster.

sentences.zh: 陳瑄之督運也，於湖廣、江西造平底淺般三千艘。

translations.literal: When Chen Xuan supervised transport, three thousand flat-bottomed shallow-draft vessels were built in Huguang and Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Xuan supervised transport, three thousand flat-bottomed shallow-draft vessels were built in Huguang and Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 二省及江、浙之米皆由江以入，至淮安新城，盤五壩過淮。

translations.literal: Grain from the two provinces and from Jiang and Zhe all entered by the river, reaching Huai'an New City, passing five dams to cross the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Grain from the two provinces and from Jiang and Zhe all entered by river, reaching Huai'an New City and passing through five dams to cross the Huai.

sentences.zh: 仁、義二壩在東門外東北，禮、智、信三壩在西門外西北，皆自城南引水抵壩口，其外即淮河。

translations.literal: The Ren and Yi dams were northeast outside the east gate; the Li, Zhi, and Xin dams were northwest outside the west gate—all drew water from south of the city to the dam mouths, beyond which lay the Huai River.
translations.idiomatic: The Ren and Yi dams stood northeast of the east gate; the Li, Zhi, and Xin dams stood northwest of the west gate. All drew water from south of the city to the dam mouths, beyond which lay the Huai River.

sentences.zh: 清江浦者，直淮城西，永樂二年嘗一修閘。

translations.literal: Qingjiangpu lies directly west of Huai'an city; in the second year of Yongle a sluice was once repaired there.
translations.idiomatic: Qingjiangpu lies directly west of Huai'an city; a sluice there was repaired once in Yongle 2.

sentences.zh: 其口淤塞，則漕船由二壩，官民商船由三壩入淮，輓輸甚勞苦。

translations.literal: When its mouth was silted up, grain-transport ships went by the two dams, while official, civilian, and merchant ships entered the Huai by the three dams—haulage was extremely arduous.
translations.idiomatic: When the mouth silted up, grain-transport ships had to use two dams while official, civilian, and merchant vessels used three dams to enter the Huai, making haulage extremely arduous.

sentences.zh: 瑄訪之故老，言：「淮城西管家湖西北，距淮河鴨陳口僅二十里，與清江口相值，宜鑿為河，引湖水通漕，宋喬維嶽所開沙河舊渠也。」

translations.literal: Xuan consulted local elders, who said: "Northwest of Guanjia Lake west of Huai'an city, only twenty li from Yachen Mouth on the Huai River and opposite Qingjiangkou—it should be excavated as a canal to draw lake water for grain transport; it is the old channel of the Sha River opened by Qiao Weiyue of the Song.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan consulted local elders, who said: "Northwest of Guanjia Lake, west of Huai'an city—only twenty li from Yachen Mouth on the Huai and opposite Qingjiangkou—a canal should be dug to draw lake water for transport. It was the old Sha River channel opened by the Song official Qiao Weiyue."

sentences.zh: 瑄乃鑿清江浦，導水由管家湖入鴨陳口達淮。

translations.literal: Xuan then excavated Qingjiangpu, channeling water from Guanjia Lake through Yachen Mouth to reach the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan then excavated Qingjiangpu, channeling water from Guanjia Lake through Yachen Mouth into the Huai.

sentences.zh: 十三年五月，工成。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the thirteenth year, the work was completed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Yongle 13, the work was completed.

sentences.zh: 緣西湖築堤亙十里以引舟。

translations.literal: A dike ten li long was built along West Lake to guide boats.
translations.idiomatic: Along West Lake a dike was built, stretching ten li to guide boats.

sentences.zh: 淮口置四閘，曰移風、清江、福興、新莊。

translations.literal: Four sluices were established at the Huai mouth, named Yifeng, Qingjiang, Fuxing, and Xinzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Four sluices were installed at the Huai mouth: Yifeng, Qingjiang, Fuxing, and Xinzhuang.

sentences.zh: 以時啟閉，嚴其禁。

translations.literal: They were opened and closed according to season, and regulations were strictly enforced.
translations.idiomatic: They were opened and closed seasonally, and restrictions were strictly enforced.

sentences.zh: 並浚儀真、瓜洲河以通江湖，鑿呂梁、百步二洪石以平水勢，開泰州白塔河以達大江。

translations.literal: They also dredged the Yizhen and Guazhou rivers to connect with the Jiang and lakes, chiseled away the rocks at the Lüliang and Baibu rapids to level the water current, and opened the Baita River at Taizhou to reach the Great River.
translations.idiomatic: They also dredged the Yizhen and Guazhou rivers to connect with the Yangtze and lakes, cut away rock at the Lüliang and Baibu rapids to tame the current, and opened Taizhou's Baita River to reach the Great River.

sentences.zh: 築高郵河堤，堤內鑿渠四十里。

translations.literal: They built dikes on the Gaoyou Canal, and within the dikes excavated a channel forty li long.
translations.idiomatic: Dikes were built on the Gaoyou Canal, and a forty-li channel was cut inside them.

sentences.zh: 久之，復置呂梁石閘，並築寶應、汜光、白馬諸湖堤，堤皆置涵洞，互相灌注。

translations.literal: After some time, the Lüliang stone sluice was restored, and dikes were also built on the Baoying, Siguang, and Baima lakes—all dikes had culverts installed to pour water into one another.
translations.idiomatic: In time the Lüliang stone sluice was restored, and dikes were built on the Baoying, Siguang, and Baima lakes as well. Every dike was fitted with culverts so water could flow between them.

sentences.zh: 是時淮上、徐州、濟寧、臨清、德州皆建倉轉輸。

translations.literal: At that time warehouses for transshipment were established at places along the Huai, Xuzhou, Jining, Linqing, and Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Warehouses for transshipment were set up along the Huai, at Xuzhou, Jining, Linqing, and Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 濱河置舍五百六十八所，舍置淺夫。

translations.literal: Five hundred sixty-eight lodges were set up along the riverbanks, each staffed with shallow-water laborers.
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred sixty-eight lodges were placed along the river, each staffed with shallow-water laborers.

sentences.zh: 水澀舟膠，俾之導行。

translations.literal: When the water was sluggish and boats stuck fast, they were made to guide passage.
translations.idiomatic: When water ran slow and boats grounded, the laborers were tasked with guiding them through.

sentences.zh: 增置淺船三千餘艘。

translations.literal: More than three thousand shallow-draft boats were added.
translations.idiomatic: More than three thousand shallow-draft boats were added to the fleet.

sentences.zh: 設徐、沛、沽頭、金溝、山東、谷亭、魯橋等閘。

translations.literal: Sluices were established at Xu, Pei, Gutou, Jingou, Shandong, Guting, Luqiao, and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Sluices were installed at Xu, Pei, Gutou, Jingou, Shandong, Guting, Luqiao, and other points.

sentences.zh: 自是漕運直達通州，而海陸運俱廢。

translations.literal: From then on grain transport reached Tongzhou directly, and both sea and land transport were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: From then on grain transport went straight to Tongzhou, and both sea and land routes were discontinued.

sentences.zh: 宣德六年用御史白圭言，浚金龍口，引河水達徐州以便漕。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xuande, following censor Bai Gui's proposal, Jinlong Mouth was dredged to lead river water to Xuzhou for the convenience of grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 6, on censor Bai Gui's advice, Jinlong Mouth was dredged to channel river water to Xuzhou for transport.

sentences.zh: 末年至英宗初再浚，並及鳳池口水，徐、呂二洪，西小河，而會通安流，自永、宣至正統間凡數十載。

translations.literal: From the end of Xuande into the early Yingzong reign it was dredged again, including Fengchi Mouth, the Xu and Lü rapids, and the West Small River—and the Huitong Canal flowed smoothly for several decades from Yongle and Xuande through the Zhengtong era.
translations.idiomatic: It was dredged again from the late Xuande period into the early Yingzong reign, extending to Fengchi Mouth, the Xu and Lü rapids, and the West Small River. The Huitong Canal ran smoothly for decades, from the Yongle and Xuande eras through Zhengtong.

sentences.zh: 至十三年，河決滎陽，東沖張秋，潰沙灣，運道始壞。

translations.literal: By the thirteenth year, the river breached at Xingyang, surged east to Zhangqiu, and broke through at Shawan—the transport route was first ruined.
translations.idiomatic: By Zhengtong 13 the river had breached at Xingyang, rushed east toward Zhangqiu, and collapsed at Shawan, damaging the transport route for the first time.

sentences.zh: 命廷臣塞之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered court officials to block it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered court officials to seal the breach.

sentences.zh: 景泰三年五月，堤工乃完。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year of Jingtai, the dike work was finally completed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Jingtai 3, the dike work was finally finished.

sentences.zh: 未匝月而北馬頭復決，掣漕流以東。

translations.literal: Not a full month passed before Beimatou breached again, drawing the grain-transport current eastward.
translations.idiomatic: Less than a month later, Beimatou breached again, pulling the transport current eastward.

sentences.zh: 清河訓導唐學成言：「河決沙灣，臨清告涸。

translations.literal: Tang Xuecheng, instructor at Qinghe, said: "The river breached at Shawan, and Linqing reported drying up.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Xuecheng, Qinghe instructor, said: "The river broke through at Shawan, and Linqing reports it is drying up.

sentences.zh: 地卑堤薄，黃河勢急，故甫完堤而復決也。

translations.literal: The ground is low and the dikes thin; the Yellow River's current is fierce—thus the dike had just been completed when it breached again.
translations.idiomatic: The terrain is low and the dikes are thin, while the Yellow River runs fast—that is why the dikes failed again as soon as they were finished.

sentences.zh: 臨清至沙灣十二閘，有水之日，其勢甚陡。

translations.literal: From Linqing to Shawan there are twelve sluices; on days when water is present, the current is very steep.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve sluices lie between Linqing and Shawan; on days when there is water, the current is extremely steep.

sentences.zh: 請於臨清以南浚月河通舟，直抵沙灣，不復由閘，則水勢緩而漕運通矣。」

translations.literal: I request dredging a bypass canal south of Linqing for boats to pass straight to Shawan, no longer passing through sluices—then the water current would be gentler and transport would flow smoothly.
translations.idiomatic: I propose dredging a bypass channel south of Linqing to allow boats to reach Shawan directly without passing through the sluices; this would slow the current and restore transport flow."

sentences.zh: 帝即命學成與山東巡撫洪英相度。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately ordered Xuecheng and Shandong grand coordinator Hong Ying to survey together.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately directed Xuecheng and Shandong grand coordinator Hong Ying to assess the site jointly.

sentences.zh: 工部侍郎趙榮則言：「沙灣抵張秋岸薄，故數決。

translations.literal: Vice-Minister of Works Zhao Rong said: "From Shawan to Zhangqiu the banks are thin, hence repeated breaches.
translations.idiomatic: Vice-Minister of Works Zhao Rong said: "Between Shawan and Zhangqiu the banks are too thin, leading to repeated breaches.

sentences.zh: 請於決處置減水石壩，使東入鹽河，則運河之水可蓄。

translations.literal: I request placing a flood-discharge stone dam at the breach site to send water east into the Salt River, so the Grand Canal water can be stored.
translations.idiomatic: A flood-discharge stone dam should be placed at the breach to divert water east into the Salt River so the canal water can be retained.

sentences.zh: 然後厚堤岸，填決口，庶無後患。」

translations.literal: Then thicken the banks, fill the breach, and perhaps there will be no further trouble afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Then reinforce the banks and block the breach to prevent future problems."

sentences.zh: 明年四月，決口方畢工，而減水壩及南分水墩先敗，已，復盡沖墩岸橋梁，決北馬頭，掣漕水入鹽河，運舟悉阻。

translations.literal: The following April, the breach work had just been completed when the flood-discharge dam and southern diversion piers failed first; afterward the pier banks, bridges, and embankments were completely washed away; Beimatou breached, drawing grain-transport water into the Salt River, and all transport boats were blocked.
translations.idiomatic: The following April, right after the breach was sealed, the flood-discharge dam and southern diversion pier collapsed first; then pier banks, bridges, and embankments were washed away entirely; Beimatou broke through, diverting canal water into the Salt River, and all transport vessels came to a halt.

sentences.zh: 教諭彭塤請立閘以制水勢，開河以分上流。

translations.literal: Instructor Peng Kun requested establishing sluices to control water flow, and opening a canal to divert the upper stream.
translations.idiomatic: Instructor Peng Kun requested building sluices to regulate the flow and excavating a canal to divert the upper reaches.

sentences.zh: 御史練綱上其策。

translations.literal: Censor Lian Gang submitted his plan to higher authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Lian Gang forwarded his proposal to the court.

sentences.zh: 詔下尚書石璞。

translations.literal: An imperial edict was issued to Minister Shi Pu.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was sent down to Minister Shi Pu.

sentences.zh: 璞乃鑿河三里，以避決口，上下與運河通。

translations.literal: Pu then dug a canal three li long to avoid the breach site, connecting upstream and downstream to the Grand Canal.
translations.idiomatic: Pu then excavated a three-li canal around the breach, linking upper and lower reaches of the Grand Canal.

sentences.zh: 是歲，漕舟不前者，命漕運總兵官徐恭姑輸東昌、濟寧倉。

translations.literal: That year, for grain boats that could not advance, grain transport commander Xu Gong was ordered to temporarily unload at the Dongchang and Jining warehouses.
translations.idiomatic: That year, transport boats unable to proceed were ordered by grain transport commander Xu Gong to temporarily offload at the Dongchang and Jining granaries.

sentences.zh: 及明年，運河膠淺如故。

translations.literal: The following year, the Grand Canal remained sluggish and shallow as before.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, the Grand Canal was still silted and shallow as before.

sentences.zh: 恭與都御史王竑言：「漕舟蟻聚臨清上下，請亟敕都御史徐有貞築塞沙灣決河。」

translations.literal: Gong and censor-in-chief Wang Hong said: "Grain boats swarm above and below Linqing like ants. We urgently request an edict ordering censor-in-chief Xu Youzhen to build up and block the Shawan breach.
translations.idiomatic: Gong and censor-in-chief Wang Hong reported: "Transport boats are backed up like ants around Linqing. We urgently request that Xu Youzhen be commanded to dam the Shawan breach."

sentences.zh: 有貞不可，而獻上三策，請置水閘，開分水河，挑運河。

translations.literal: Youzhen declined, but offered three plans to the throne: establish water sluices, open a diversion canal, and dredge the Grand Canal.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhen refused the direct order but submitted three proposals: install water gates, excavate a diversion channel, and dredge the canal.

sentences.zh: 六年三月，詔羣臣集議方略。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixth year, an edict ordered officials to assemble and deliberate on strategy.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Tianshun 6, officials were summoned to discuss strategy together.

sentences.zh: 工部尚書江淵等請用官軍五萬以浚運。

translations.literal: Works Minister Jiang Yuan and others requested deploying fifty thousand government troops to dredge transport.
translations.idiomatic: Works Minister Jiang Yuan and others asked to deploy fifty thousand troops to dredge the canal.

sentences.zh: 有貞恐役軍費重，請復陳瑄舊制，置撈淺夫，用沿河州縣民，免其役。

translations.literal: Youzhen feared the cost of conscripting troops would be heavy and requested restoring Chen Xuan's old system—establish dredging laborers, using people from counties along the river and exempting them from corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhen worried that mobilizing troops would be too costly and urged reviving Chen Xuan's old practice: recruit dredging laborers from riverside counties and exempt them from corvée duties.

sentences.zh: 五月，浚漕工竣。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, dredging of the grain route was completed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, canal dredging was finished.

sentences.zh: 七月，沙灣決口工亦竣，會通復安。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, the Shawan breach work was also completed, and the Huitong Canal was restored to peaceful flow.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, work on the Shawan breach was completed as well, and the Huitong Canal ran smoothly again.

sentences.zh: 都御史陳泰一浚淮、揚漕河，築口置壩。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Chen Tai dredged the Huai-Yang grain canal and built mouths and dams.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Chen Tai dredged the Huai-Yang transport canal and built intake works and dams.

sentences.zh: 黃河嘗灌新莊閘至清江浦三十餘里，淤淺阻漕，稍稍浚治，即復其舊。

translations.literal: The Yellow River once flooded over thirty li from Xinzhuang Sluice to Qingjiangpu, silting and shoaling to block grain transport—a little dredging restored it to its former state.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River once inundated the thirty-plus li from Xinzhuang Sluice to Qingjiangpu, silting the channel and blocking transport; gradual dredging brought it back to normal.

sentences.zh: 英宗初，命官督漕，分濟寧南北為二，侍郎鄭辰治其南，副都御史賈諒治其北。

translations.literal: Early in Yingzong's reign, officials were appointed to supervise grain transport; Jining was divided into south and north—Vice-Minister Zheng Chen managed the south, vice censor-in-chief Jia Liang the north.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yingzong's reign, officials were appointed to oversee transport, with Jining split into north and south sections—Vice-Minister Zheng Chen handled the south and vice censor-in-chief Jia Liang the north.

sentences.zh: 成化七年，又因廷議，分漕河沛縣以南、德州以北及山東為三道，各委曹郎及監司專理，且請簡風力大臣總理其事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Chenghua, following court deliberation, the grain canal south of Pei County and north of Dezhou and Shandong were divided into three sections, each entrusted to a bureau director and regional inspector for dedicated management—and a request was made to select a forceful senior official to oversee the whole.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 7, after court discussion, the canal south of Pei County, north of Dezhou, and Shandong were split into three districts, each assigned to a bureau director and supervising official, with a request to appoint a senior minister of proven ability as overall supervisor.

sentences.zh: 始命侍郎王恕為總河。

translations.literal: Wang Shu was first appointed vice minister as Grand Canal overseer.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu was first appointed Vice-Minister and Grand Canal overseer.

sentences.zh: 二十一年敕工部侍郎杜謙浚運道，自通州至淮、揚，會山東、河南撫按相度經理。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year an edict ordered Works Vice-Minister Du Qian to dredge the transport route from Tongzhou to Huai-Yang, coordinating with Shandong and Henan grand coordinators and regional inspectors to survey and manage.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 21, Works Vice-Minister Du Qian was ordered to dredge the transport route from Tongzhou to Huai-Yang, working with Shandong and Henan grand coordinators and regional inspectors on survey and management.

sentences.zh: 弘治二年，河復決張秋，沖會通河，命戶部侍郎白昂相治。

translations.literal: In the second year of Hongzhi, the river again breached at Zhangqiu, surging into the Huitong Canal—the emperor ordered Revenue Vice-Minister Bai Ang to oversee the repairs jointly.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 2, the river breached again at Zhangqiu and flooded into the Huitong Canal; Revenue Vice-Minister Bai Ang was ordered to take charge of repairs.

sentences.zh: 昂奏金龍口決口已淤，河並為一大支，由祥符合沁下徐州而去。

translations.literal: Ang reported that the Jinlong Mouth breach had already silted up, and the river had merged into one large branch flowing from Xiangfu via the Qin River down past Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ang reported that the Jinlong Mouth breach had already silted shut and that the river had united into a single channel descending from Xiangfu along the Qin River toward Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 其間河道淺隘，宜於所經七縣，築堤岸以衛張秋。

translations.literal: The channel in between was shallow and narrow; dikes should be built in the seven counties it passed through to protect Zhangqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Along the route the channel was shallow and constricted; dikes should be raised in the seven counties traversed to safeguard Zhangqiu.

sentences.zh: 下工部議，從其請。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the Ministry of Works for deliberation, and his request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was sent to the Ministry of Works for review and approved.

sentences.zh: 昂又以漕船經高郵甓社湖多溺，請於堤東開複河西四十里以通舟。

translations.literal: Ang also noted that grain boats frequently sank crossing Gaoyou's Bishe Lake, and requested opening a parallel canal forty li west of the eastern dike for boat passage.
translations.idiomatic: Ang also reported that transport boats often sank on Gaoyou's Bishe Lake and asked that a parallel canal forty li west of the eastern dike be opened for navigation.

sentences.zh: 越四年，河復決數道入運河，壞張秋東堤，奪汶水入海，漕流絕。

translations.literal: Four years later, the river breached in several places into the Grand Canal, destroying the eastern dike at Zhangqiu, seizing the Wen River current to the sea—grain transport was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later the river broke through again in several places into the canal, wrecked the eastern dike at Zhangqiu, diverted the Wen River toward the sea, and cut off transport entirely.

sentences.zh: 時工部侍郎陳政總理河道，集夫十五萬，治未效而卒。

translations.literal: At that time Works Vice-Minister Chen Zheng oversaw river management; he gathered one hundred fifty thousand laborers but died before the work took effect.
translations.idiomatic: Works Vice-Minister Chen Zheng was then in charge of the waterways; he mobilized 150,000 laborers but died before the project succeeded.

sentences.zh: 六年春，副都御史劉大夏奉敕往治決河。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year, Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu Daxia received an edict to go repair the breached river.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Hongzhi 6, Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu Daxia was ordered to go block the breach.

sentences.zh: 夏半，漕舟鱗集，乃先自決口西岸鑿月河以通漕。

translations.literal: By midsummer, grain boats had gathered densely; he first excavated a bypass canal from the west bank of the breach to restore grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: By midsummer transport boats had piled up thickly; he first cut a bypass channel from the west bank of the breach to restore traffic.

sentences.zh: 經營二年，張秋決口就塞，復築黃陵岡上流。

translations.literal: After two years of effort, the Zhangqiu breach was blocked, and the upstream works at Huangling Gang were rebuilt.
translations.idiomatic: After two years of work the Zhangqiu breach was sealed and the upper works at Huangling Gang were rebuilt.

sentences.zh: 於是河復南下，運道無阻。

translations.literal: Thus the river flowed south again, and the transport route was unobstructed.
translations.idiomatic: The river then resumed its southward course and the transport route was clear again.

sentences.zh: 乃改張秋曰安平鎮，建廟賜額曰顯惠神祠，命大學士王鏊紀其事，勒於石。

translations.literal: Zhangqiu was renamed Anping Town; a temple was built and granted the title Xianhui Shrine; Grand Secretary Wang Ao was ordered to record the event and inscribe it on stone.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangqiu was renamed Anping Town, a temple was built and titled the Xianhui Shrine, and Grand Secretary Wang Ao was commissioned to commemorate the feat in an inscription on stone.

sentences.zh: 而白昂所開高郵複河亦成，賜名康濟，其西岸以石甃之。

translations.literal: The parallel canal Bai Ang had opened at Gaoyou was also completed, granted the name Kangji, and its west bank was faced with stone.
translations.idiomatic: The parallel canal Bai Ang had opened at Gaoyou was finished as well, named the Kangji Canal, with its west bank revetted in stone.

sentences.zh: 又甃高郵堤，自杭家閘至張家鎮凡三十里。

translations.literal: The Gaoyou dikes were also faced with stone from Hangjia Sluice to Zhangjia Town—a total of thirty li.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaoyou dikes were also revetted in stone from Hangjia Sluice to Zhangjia Town, thirty li in all.

sentences.zh: 高郵堤者，洪武時所築也。

translations.literal: The Gaoyou dikes were built in the Hongwu era.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaoyou dikes dated from the Hongwu period.

sentences.zh: 陳瑄因舊增築，延及寶應，土人相沿謂之老堤。

translations.literal: Chen Xuan built them up on the old foundations, extending to Baoying—the locals have since called them the Old Dikes.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xuan expanded them on the old foundations, extending as far as Baoying; locals have long called them the Old Dikes.

sentences.zh: 正統三年易土以石。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengtong, earth was replaced with stone.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 3, earthen sections were replaced with stone.

sentences.zh: 成化時，遣官築重堤於高郵、邵伯、寶應、白馬四湖老堤之東。

translations.literal: During Chenghua, officials were dispatched to build heavy dikes east of the Old Dikes on the four lakes of Gaoyou, Shaobo, Baoying, and Baima.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chenghua reign, officials were sent to build secondary dikes east of the Old Dikes on the four lakes: Gaoyou, Shaobo, Baoying, and Baima.

sentences.zh: 而王恕為總河，修淮安以南諸決堤，且浚淮、揚漕河。

translations.literal: Wang Shu, as Grand Canal overseer, repaired various breached dikes south of Huai'an and also dredged the Huai-Yang grain canal.
translations.idiomatic: As Grand Canal overseer, Wang Shu repaired breached dikes south of Huai'an and dredged the Huai-Yang transport canal.

sentences.zh: 重湖鵒需民盜決溉田之罰，造閘鵜達以儲湖水。

translations.literal: He strengthened the lake dikes, strictly enforced penalties on those who illicitly breached dikes to irrigate fields, and built sluices and dams to store lake water.
translations.idiomatic: He reinforced the lake dikes, imposed strict penalties on illegal dike breaches for irrigation, and built sluice gates and dams to hold lake water in reserve.

sentences.zh: 及大夏塞張秋，而昂又開康濟，漕河上下無大患者二十餘年。

translations.literal: After Daxia blocked Zhangqiu and Ang opened Kangji, the grain canal above and below had no major disasters for more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Daxia sealed Zhangqiu and Bai Ang opened the Kangji Canal, the transport route suffered no major calamity for more than twenty years.

sentences.zh: 十六年，巡撫徐源言：「濟寧地最高，必引上源洸水以濟，其口在堈城石瀨之上。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, grand coordinator Xu Yuan said: "Jining is at the highest elevation; upper-source Guang River water must be drawn to supply it—the intake lies above the Gangcheng stony rapid.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 16, grand coordinator Xu Yuan said: "Jining sits at the highest point and must be fed from the upper Guang River; the intake is above the Gangcheng stony rapid.

sentences.zh: 元時治閘作堰，使水盡入南旺，分濟南北運。

translations.literal: In Yuan times sluices and dams were managed so that all water entered Nanwang, divided to supply north and south transport.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuan, sluices and dams were managed to channel all water into Nanwang, divided to serve northbound and southbound transport.

sentences.zh: 成化間，易土以石。

translations.literal: During Chenghua, earth was replaced with stone.
translations.idiomatic: During Chenghua, the earthen works were converted to stone.

sentences.zh: 夫土堰之利，水小則遏以入洮，水大則閉閘以防沙壅，聽其漫堰西流。

translations.literal: The advantage of earthen dams: when water is low they hold it back to enter the Guang River; when water is high the sluices are closed to prevent sand blockage, allowing overflow west over the dam.
translations.idiomatic: The benefit of earthen dams was that in low water they held the flow back into the Guang River, while in high water the sluices were shut to keep out silt, letting surplus water spill west over the dam.

sentences.zh: 自石堰成，水遂橫溢，石堰既壞，民田亦沖。

translations.literal: Since the stone dam was built, water has overflowed everywhere; once the stone dam broke, farmland was also washed away.
translations.idiomatic: After the stone dam went up, water spread uncontrollably; when it collapsed, farmland was swept away as well.

sentences.zh: 洸河沙塞，雖有閘門，壓不能啟。

translations.literal: The Guang River is sand-choked; though there are sluice gates, pressure prevents opening them.
translations.idiomatic: The Guang River was choked with sand; even though sluice gates existed, sediment pressure kept them from opening.

sentences.zh: 乞毀石復土，疏洸口壅塞以至濟寧，而築堈城迤西春城口子決岸。」

translations.literal: I beg to demolish the stone and restore earth, dredge the Guang River mouth blockage through to Jining, and build up the breached bank at Chuncheng Mouth west of Gangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the stone structure be removed and earthen dams restored, that the blocked Guang River mouth be dredged through to Jining, and that the breached bank at Chuncheng Mouth west of Gangcheng be repaired."

sentences.zh: 帝命侍郎李遂往勘，言：「堈城石堰，一可遏淤沙，不為南旺湖之害，一可殺水勢，不慮戴村壩之沖，不宜毀。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Vice-Minister Li Sui to investigate; he said: "The Gangcheng stone dam can, first, hold back silting sand without harm to Nanwang Lake, and second, reduce water force without fear of damage to Daicun Dam—it should not be demolished.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Vice-Minister Li Sui to investigate. He reported: "The Gangcheng stone dam blocks silt without harming Nanwang Lake and reduces the current without threatening Daicun Dam—it should not be torn down.

sentences.zh: 近堰積沙，宜浚。

translations.literal: Sand has accumulated near the dam and should be dredged.
translations.idiomatic: Silt had piled up near the dam and should be cleared.

sentences.zh: 堈城稍東有元時舊閘，引洸水入濟寧，下接徐、呂漕河。

translations.literal: Slightly east of Gangcheng is an old Yuan-era sluice that draws Guang River water into Jining, connecting downstream with the Xu and Lü grain canal.
translations.idiomatic: Just east of Gangcheng stood an old Yuan sluice that diverted Guang River water into Jining and linked downstream to the Xu and Lü transport canal.

sentences.zh: 東平州戴村，則汶水入海故道也。

translations.literal: Daicun in Dongping Prefecture is the old course by which the Wen River reached the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Daicun in Dongping Prefecture was the Wen River's old route to the sea.

sentences.zh: 自永樂初，橫築一壩，遏汶入南旺湖，漕河始通。

translations.literal: Since the early Yongle era, a transverse dam was built to hold the Wen into Nanwang Lake—and only then did the grain canal open.
translations.idiomatic: From early Yongle onward a cross dam held the Wen into Nanwang Lake, which is what first opened the transport canal.

sentences.zh: 今自分水龍王廟至天井閘九十里，水高三丈有奇，若洸河更浚而深，則汶流盡向濟甯而南，臨清河道必涸。

translations.literal: Today from the Fenlongwang Temple Dividing Point to Tianjing Sluice spans ninety li, with water more than three zhang deep—if the Guang River were dredged deeper still, the Wen current would all flow south toward Jining, and the Linqing channel must dry up.
translations.idiomatic: From the Fenlongwang Dividing Temple to Tianjing Sluice is ninety li, with water over three zhang deep; dredging the Guang River deeper would send the entire Wen flow south toward Jining and leave the Linqing reach dry.

sentences.zh: 洸口不可浚。

translations.literal: The Guang River mouth must not be dredged.
translations.idiomatic: The Guang River mouth should not be dredged.

sentences.zh: 堈城口至柳泉九十里，無關運道，可弗事。

translations.literal: From Gangcheng Mouth to Liuquan is ninety li—unrelated to the transport route and need not be attended to.
translations.idiomatic: The ninety li from Gangcheng Mouth to Liuquan does not affect transport and can be left alone.

sentences.zh: 柳泉至濟寧，汶、泗諸水會流處，宜疏者二十餘里。

translations.literal: From Liuquan to Jining, where the Wen, Si, and other waters converge, some twenty-plus li should be dredged.
translations.idiomatic: From Liuquan to Jining, where the Wen, Si, and other streams meet, about twenty li needs dredging.

sentences.zh: 春城口，外障汶水，內防民田，堤卑岸薄，宜與戴村壩並修築。」

translations.literal: Chuncheng Mouth, blocking Wen water outward and protecting farmland within—the dikes are low and banks thin; it should be repaired together with Daicun Dam.
translations.idiomatic: At Chuncheng Mouth, which holds back Wen water on the outside and protects farmland within, the dikes are low and the banks weak; it should be rebuilt together with Daicun Dam."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: His recommendation was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved his report.

sentences.zh: 正德四年十月，河決沛縣飛雲橋，入運。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fourth year of Zhengde, the river breached at Feiyun Bridge in Pei County and entered the Grand Canal.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Zhengde 4, the river broke through at Feiyun Bridge in Pei County and flooded into the canal.

sentences.zh: 尋塞。

translations.literal: It was soon blocked.
translations.idiomatic: The breach was soon sealed.

sentences.zh: 世宗之初，河數壞漕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign, the river repeatedly damaged grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiajing reign, repeated river breaches disrupted transport.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖六年，光祿少卿黃綰論泉源之利，言：「漕河泉源皆發山東南旺、馬場、樊村、安山諸湖。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiajing, Chamberlain for Ceremonials Huang Wan discussed the benefit of spring sources, saying: "The spring sources of the grain canal all rise from the Shandong lakes of Nanwang, Machang, Fancun, and Anshan.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 6, Ceremonial Chamberlain Huang Wan argued for harnessing spring sources, saying: "The canal's springs all issue from Shandong's Nanwang, Machang, Fancun, and Anshan lakes.

sentences.zh: 泉水所鐘，亟宜修浚，且引他泉並蓄，則漕不竭。

translations.literal: Where springs gather, dredging is urgently needed—and if other springs are also drawn and stored, grain transport will never run dry.
translations.idiomatic: The spring basins urgently need dredging; if additional springs are tapped and pooled, transport water will not fail.

sentences.zh: 南旺、馬場堤外孫村地窪，若瀦為湖，改作漕道，尤可免濟甯高原淺澀之苦。」

translations.literal: Sun Village outside the Nanwang and Machang dikes sits in low ground; if impounded as a lake and converted to a grain route, it would especially relieve Jining's high-plateau shallow-water hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Village, low ground outside the Nanwang and Machang dikes, could be dammed into a lake and made a transport channel, easing Jining's chronic shallow water on the high ground."

sentences.zh: 帝命總河侍郎章拯議。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Grand Canal Vice-Minister Zhang Zheng to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Grand Canal Vice-Minister Zhang Zheng to study the proposal.

sentences.zh: 而拯以黃水入運，運船阻沛上，方為御史吳仲所劾。

translations.literal: But Zheng, because Yellow River water had entered the canal and transport boats were blocked above Pei, was being impeached by censor Wu Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zheng was meanwhile under impeachment by censor Wu Zhong for allowing Yellow River water into the canal and blocking transport boats above Pei County.

sentences.zh: 拯言：「河塞難遽通，惟金溝口迤北新沖一渠可令運船由此入昭陽湖，出沙河板橋。

translations.literal: Zheng said: "The blocked river cannot be quickly reopened; only the newly breached channel north of Jingou Mouth can allow transport boats to enter Zhaoyang Lake by it and exit at Shahe Banqiao.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng replied: "The river cannot be reopened quickly; only the newly cut channel north of Jingou Mouth can let transport boats pass into Zhaoyang Lake and exit at Shahe Banqiao.

sentences.zh: 其先阻淺者，則西曆雞鵒塚寺，出廟道北口通行。」

translations.literal: Those blocked earlier by shoals should go west past Jigu Tumu Temple and exit via the north mouth of the temple road.
translations.idiomatic: Where shoals blocked passage earlier, boats should go west past Jigu Tumu Temple and leave through the north outlet of the temple road."

sentences.zh: 下部並議，未決。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the ministries for joint deliberation, but no decision was reached.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal went to the ministries for joint review, but no decision was made.

sentences.zh: 給事中張嵩言：「昭陽湖地庳，河勢高，引河灌湖，必致彌漫，使湖道復阻。

translations.literal: Censor Zhang Song said: "Zhaoyang Lake sits low, while the river stands high; diverting the river to flood the lake will inevitably spread water everywhere and block the lake route again.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhang Song argued: "Zhaoyang Lake lies in low ground and the river runs higher; if the river is led in to fill the lake, the water will spread unchecked and the lake passage will be blocked again.

sentences.zh: 請罷拯，別推大臣。」

translations.literal: I ask that Zheng be dismissed and another senior minister be put forward."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that Zhang Zheng be removed and a different senior minister be appointed."

sentences.zh: 部議如嵩言。

translations.literal: The ministries deliberated and agreed with Song.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries reviewed the proposal and endorsed Zhang Song's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 拯再疏自劾，乞罷，不許。

translations.literal: Zheng memorialized again impeaching himself and begging dismissal, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zheng submitted another memorial impeaching himself and asking to be relieved, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 卒引運船道湖中。

translations.literal: In the end transport boats were routed through the lake.
translations.idiomatic: Transport boats were ultimately sent through the lake after all.

sentences.zh: 其冬，詔拯還京別敘，而命擇大臣督理。

translations.literal: That winter an edict recalled Zheng to the capital for separate appointment and ordered that a senior minister be chosen to supervise the work.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the emperor ordered Zhang Zheng back to the capital for reassignment and directed that a senior minister be selected to take charge.

sentences.zh: 諸大臣多進治河議。

translations.literal: Many senior ministers submitted proposals on river control.
translations.idiomatic: Senior ministers submitted numerous plans for managing the rivers.

sentences.zh: 詹事霍韜謂：「前議役山東、河南丁夫數萬，疏浚淤沙以通運。

translations.literal: Household Tutor Huo Tao said: "The earlier proposal was to conscript tens of thousands of laborers from Shandong and Henan to dredge silt and sand and open transport.
translations.idiomatic: Household Tutor Huo Tao said: "The earlier plan called for tens of thousands of corvée laborers from Shandong and Henan to dredge silt and reopen transport.

sentences.zh: 然沙隨水下，旋浚旋淤。

translations.literal: Yet sand follows the water down; no sooner is it dredged than it silts up again.
translations.idiomatic: But sand settles as fast as the water moves—dredge today and it silts again tomorrow.

sentences.zh: 今運舟由昭陽湖入雞鳴臺至沙河，迂迴不過百里。

translations.literal: Today transport boats enter Zhaoyang Lake at Jiming Terrace and reach Shahe—a detour of no more than one hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: At present transport boats pass from Zhaoyang Lake through Jiming Terrace to Shahe, a roundabout route of less than one hundred li.

sentences.zh: 若沿湖築堤，浚為小河，河口為閘，以待蓄泄，水溢可避風濤，水涸易為疏浚。

translations.literal: If dikes are built along the lake, a small channel dredged, and sluices placed at the mouth to store and release water, overflow can be sheltered from wind and waves, and when water runs low dredging is easy.
translations.idiomatic: If dikes were built along the lake shore, the channel dredged into a narrow canal, and sluice gates set at the mouth to hold and release water, high water could be kept clear of wind and waves, and low water would be easy to dredge.

sentences.zh: 三月而土堤成，一年而石堤成，用力少，取效速。

translations.literal: In three months the earthen dikes would be finished, in one year the stone dikes—little labor, quick results.
translations.idiomatic: Earthen dikes could be finished in three months and stone dikes in a year, with less labor and faster results.

sentences.zh: 黃河愈溢，運道愈利，較之役丁夫以浚淤土，勞逸大不侔也。」

translations.literal: The more the Yellow River overflows, the more the transport route benefits—compared with conscripting laborers to dredge silt, the difference in toil and ease is vast."
translations.idiomatic: The higher the Yellow River ran, the better the transport route would fare—far less burdensome than mobilizing corvée labor to dredge silt by hand."

sentences.zh: 尚書李承勳謂：「於昭陽湖左別開一河，引諸泉為運道，自留城沙河為尤便。」

translations.literal: Minister Li Chengxun said: "Cut a separate channel to the left of Zhaoyang Lake, draw the various springs as the transport route—starting from Liucheng and Shahe would be especially convenient."
translations.idiomatic: Minister Li Chengxun proposed: "Open a new channel on the west side of Zhaoyang Lake and use the spring waters as the transport route; routing it from Liucheng and Shahe would be especially convenient."

sentences.zh: 與都御史胡世寧議合。

translations.literal: His view accorded with Censor-in-Chief Hu Shining's.
translations.idiomatic: This matched the plan of Censor-in-Chief Hu Shining.

sentences.zh: 七年正月，總河都御史盛應期奏如世寧策，請於昭陽湖東鑿新河，自汪家口南出留城口，長百四十里，刻期六月畢工。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year, Grand Canal Censor-in-Chief Sheng Yingqi memorialized adopting Hu Shining's plan, asking to cut a new channel east of Zhaoyang Lake from Wangjiakou south to Liucheng Mouth, one hundred forty li long, with a fixed deadline of completion in the sixth month.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Jiajing 7, Grand Canal Censor-in-Chief Sheng Yingqi submitted a memorial adopting Hu Shining's plan, proposing to cut a new channel east of Zhaoyang Lake from Wangjiakou south to Liucheng Mouth—a distance of one hundred forty li, to be finished by the sixth month.

sentences.zh: 工未半，而應期罷去，役遂已。

translations.literal: Before half the work was done, Yingqi was dismissed and the labor ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Before the project was half finished, Sheng Yingqi was removed from office and the work stopped.

sentences.zh: 其後三十年，硃衡始循其遺跡，浚而成之。

translations.literal: Thirty years later Zhu Heng at last followed its traces, dredged, and completed it.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty years later Zhu Heng finally traced the old line, dredged it, and brought the channel to completion.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，總河侍郎潘希會加築濟、沛間東西兩堤，以拒黃河。

translations.literal: That winter Grand Canal Vice-Minister Pan Xihui further built the eastern and western dikes between Jining and Pei to repel the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Grand Canal Vice-Minister Pan Xihui strengthened the eastern and western dikes between Jining and Pei County to hold back the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 十九年七月，河決野雞岡，二洪涸。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the nineteenth year the river breached at Yeji Hill and the two rapids ran dry.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Jiajing 19 the river broke through at Yeji Hill and the Xu and Lü rapids dried up.

sentences.zh: 督理河漕侍郎王以旂請浚山東諸泉以濟運，且築長堤聚水，如閘河制。

translations.literal: Grand Canal Supervisor Vice-Minister Wang Yiqiao asked to dredge Shandong's springs to supply transport, and also to build long dikes to impound water, as on the Sluice River.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Canal Supervisor Vice-Minister Wang Yiqiao proposed dredging Shandong's springs to feed transport and building long dikes to store water, following the Sluice River model.

sentences.zh: 遂清舊泉百七十八，開新泉三十一。

translations.literal: Accordingly one hundred seventy-eight old springs were cleared and thirty-one new ones opened.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred seventy-eight existing springs were cleared and thirty-one new ones opened.

sentences.zh: 以旂復奏四事。

translations.literal: Yiqiao memorialized again with four proposals.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yiqiao submitted a further memorial outlining four measures.

sentences.zh: 一請以諸泉分隸守土官兼理其事，毋使堙塞。

translations.literal: First, he asked that the springs be assigned to local officials for concurrent management so they would not be blocked.
translations.idiomatic: First, he asked that the springs be placed under local officials for ongoing upkeep so they would not silt shut.

sentences.zh: 一請於境山鎮、徐、呂二洪之下，各建石閘，蓄水數尺以行舟，旁留月河以泄暴汛；

translations.literal: Second, he asked that below Jingshan Town and the Xu and Lü rapids stone sluices be built at each site, storing several chi of water for boat passage, with bypass channels left beside them to discharge sudden floods;
translations.idiomatic: Second, he proposed stone sluices below Jingshan Town and at the Xu and Lü rapids, each holding several chi of water for navigation, with parallel relief channels beside them to spill flood surges;

sentences.zh: 築四木閘於武家溝、小河口、石城、匙頭灣，而置方船於沙坊等淺，以備撈浚。

translations.literal: four wooden sluices built at Wujiagou, Xiaohekou, Shicheng, and Shitou Bay, and square barges placed at shoals such as Shafang for dredging.
translations.idiomatic: four timber sluices at Wujiagou, Xiaohekou, Shicheng, and Shitou Bay, and square dredging barges stationed at shoals such as Shafang.

sentences.zh: 一言漕河兩岸有南旺、安山、馬場、昭陽四湖，名為水櫃，所以匯諸泉濟漕河也。

translations.literal: Third, he said that on both banks of the grain canal are the four lakes of Nanwang, Anshan, Machang, and Zhaoyang, called water reservoirs, which gather the springs to supply the canal.
translations.idiomatic: Third, he noted that Nanwang, Anshan, Machang, and Zhaoyang—the four lakes flanking the canal, known as water reservoirs—were meant to collect spring water for the transport route.

sentences.zh: 豪強侵佔，蓄水不多，而昭陽一湖淤成高地，大非國初設湖初意。

translations.literal: Powerful families encroached, little water was stored, and Zhaoyang Lake alone silted into high ground—far from the original intent when the lakes were first established.
