translations.idiomatic: Local magnates had encroached on them, storage had dwindled, and Zhaoyang Lake in particular had silted up into high ground—a far cry from the purpose for which the lakes were created at the dynasty's founding.

sentences.zh: 宜委官清理，添置閘、壩、斗門，培築堤岸，多開溝渠，浚深河底，以復四櫃。

translations.literal: Officials should be appointed to clear them, add sluices, dams, and wicket gates, raise and build dikes and banks, open more ditches and channels, and dredge the river bottom deep, to restore the four reservoirs.
translations.idiomatic: He urged appointing officials to reclaim the lakes, add sluices, dams, and wicket gates, rebuild the dikes, open additional channels, and dredge the bed deeper to restore all four reservoirs.

sentences.zh: 一言黃河南徙，舊閘口俱塞，惟孫繼一口獨存。

translations.literal: Fourth, he said that when the Yellow River shifted south, the old sluice mouths were all blocked—only Sunji Mouth alone remained.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, he reported that after the Yellow River moved south, the old sluice openings had all silted shut—only Sunji Mouth remained open.

sentences.zh: 導河出徐州小浮橋，下徐、呂二洪，此濟運之大者。

translations.literal: Guiding the river out at Xuzhou's Small Floating Bridge and down through the Xu and Lü rapids—this is the great means of supplying transport.
translations.idiomatic: Directing the river out at Xuzhou's Small Floating Bridge and down through the Xu and Lü rapids was the chief way to keep transport supplied.

sentences.zh: 請於孫繼口多開一溝，及時疏瀹，庶二洪得濟。

translations.literal: He asked that at Sunji Mouth another ditch be opened and dredged in good time, so that the two rapids might be supplied.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that an additional channel be cut at Sunji Mouth and dredged promptly so the two rapids could be fed.

sentences.zh: 帝可其奏，而以管泉專責之部曹。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his memorial, but assigned sole responsibility for managing the springs to a ministry bureau.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the memorial but placed sole responsibility for the springs with a ministry bureau.

sentences.zh: 徐、呂二洪者，河漕咽喉也。

translations.literal: The Xu and Lü rapids are the throat of the river grain route.
translations.idiomatic: The Xu and Lü rapids were the choke point of the canal transport system.

sentences.zh: 自陳瑄鑿石疏渠，正統初，復浚洪西小河。

translations.literal: Since Chen Xuan cut stone and dredged channels, at the beginning of Zhengtong the small river west of the rapids was dredged again.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Chen Xuan cut stone and opened channels, the small river west of the rapids was dredged again early in the Zhengtong reign.

sentences.zh: 漕運參將湯節又以洪迅敗舟，於上流築堰，逼水歸月河，河南建閘以蓄水勢。

translations.literal: Grain Transport Deputy Commander Tang Jie, because the rapids' swift current wrecked boats, built a dam upstream forcing water into the bypass channel, and on the south bank built sluices to store the water's force.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy Commander Tang Jie of grain transport, finding that the swift current at the rapids wrecked boats, built an upstream dam to drive water into the bypass channel and erected sluices on the south bank to impound the flow.

sentences.zh: 成化四年，管河主簿郭升以大石築兩堤，錮以鐵錠，鑿外洪敗船惡石三百，而平築裏洪堤岸，又甃石岸東西四百餘丈。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chenghua, River Registrar Guo Sheng built both dikes with great stones, locked with iron bolts, chiseled away three hundred wrecking rocks from the outer rapid, leveled and built the inner rapid's dikes and banks, and faced four hundred-plus zhang of stone banks east and west.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 4, River Registrar Guo Sheng built both dikes of large stone secured with iron bolts, removed three hundred wrecking rocks from the outer rapid, leveled and rebuilt the inner rapid's banks, and faced more than four hundred zhang of shoreline with stone on both sides.

sentences.zh: 十六年增甃呂梁洪石堤、石壩二百餘丈，以資牽挽。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year stone dikes and stone dams at Lüliang Rapid were further faced for two hundred-plus zhang to aid hauling.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 16, more than two hundred zhang of stone dikes and dams were added at Lüliang Rapid to support boat hauling.

sentences.zh: 及是建閘，行者益便之。

translations.literal: When sluices were built at this time, travelers found passage even more convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Once the sluices were built, passage became still easier.

sentences.zh: 四十四年七月，河大決沛縣，漫昭陽湖，由沙河至二洪，浩渺無際，運道淤塞百餘里。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the forty-fourth year the river breached greatly at Pei County, flooded Zhaoyang Lake, and from Shahe to the two rapids spread boundlessly; the transport route silted shut for more than one hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Jiajing 44 the river broke catastrophically at Pei County, inundated Zhaoyang Lake, and from Shahe to the two rapids spread without limit; the transport route was blocked for more than one hundred li.

sentences.zh: 督理河漕尚書硃衡循覽盛應期所鑿新河遺跡，請開南陽、留城上下。

translations.literal: Grand Canal Supervisor Minister Zhu Heng traced the remains of the new channel cut by Sheng Yingqi and asked to open it above and below Nanyang and Liucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Canal Supervisor Minister Zhu Heng surveyed the remains of the new channel Sheng Yingqi had cut and proposed opening it above and below Nanyang and Liucheng.

sentences.zh: 總河都御史潘季馴不可。

translations.literal: Grand Canal Censor-in-Chief Pan Jixun objected.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Canal Censor-in-Chief Pan Jixun opposed the plan.

sentences.zh: 衡言：「是河直秦溝，有所束隘。

translations.literal: Heng said: "That channel runs straight to Qin Ditch and is in places constricted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Heng replied: "That channel runs straight toward Qin Ditch and is pinched in places.

sentences.zh: 伏秋黃水盛，昭陽受之，不為壑也。」

translations.literal: In the flood season when Yellow River water runs high, Zhaoyang receives it and does not become a spillway basin."
translations.idiomatic: During the flood season, when Yellow River water runs high, Zhaoyang can take it in without becoming an uncontrolled spillway."

sentences.zh: 乃決計開浚，身自督工，重懲不用命者。

translations.literal: He then resolved to open and dredge it, personally supervised the work, and punished disobedience severely.
translations.idiomatic: He decided to proceed with opening and dredging the channel, supervised the work in person, and punished anyone who failed to obey orders.

sentences.zh: 給事中鄭欽劾衡故興難成之役，虐民幸功。

translations.literal: Censor Zheng Qin impeached Heng for deliberately launching a hard-to-finish project, abusing the people while seeking credit.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zheng Qin impeached Zhu Heng for launching a project doomed to fail, oppressing the people while chasing glory.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣官勘新舊河孰利。

translations.literal: The court dispatched officials to survey which of the old and new channels was more advantageous.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent officials to inspect whether the old or new channel would serve better.

sentences.zh: 給事中何起鳴勘河還，言：「舊河難復有五，而新河之難成者亦有三。

translations.literal: Censor He Qiming returned from surveying the river and said: "There are five reasons the old channel is hard to restore, and three reasons the new channel is hard to complete.
translations.idiomatic: Censor He Qiming returned from inspecting the river and reported: "There are five obstacles to restoring the old channel and three to finishing the new one.

sentences.zh: 顧新河多舊堤高阜，黃水難侵，睃而通之，運道必利。

translations.literal: Yet the new channel has many old dikes and high mounds; Yellow River water can hardly invade it—clear it and open passage, and the transport route must benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Still, the new route runs along old dikes and high ground where Yellow River water cannot easily reach; open it up and transport will surely improve.

sentences.zh: 所謂三難者，一以夏村迤北地高，恐難接水，然地勢高低，大約不過二丈，一視水準加深，何患水淺。

translations.literal: The so-called three difficulties: first, north of Xiacun the ground is high and water may be hard to connect—but the rise and fall is roughly no more than two zhang; adjust the water level deeper and what fear of shallow water?
translations.idiomatic: Of the three difficulties: first, the ground north of Xiacun is high and may be hard to feed—but the elevation change is only about two zhang; deepen the channel to the proper level and shallow water need not be feared.

sentences.zh: 一以三河口積沙深厚，水勢湍急，不無阻塞，然建壩攔截，歲一挑浚之，何患沙壅。

translations.literal: Second, at Sanhe Mouth sand has piled deep and the current runs swift—blockage is not impossible; yet build a dam to intercept it and dredge once a year—what fear of sand clogging?
translations.idiomatic: Second, at Sanhe Mouth sand has piled deep and the current runs fast, which could cause blockage—but build a dam to trap it and dredge once a year, and sand buildup need not be feared.

sentences.zh: 一以馬家橋築堤，微山取土不便，又恐水口投埽，勢必不堅，然使委任得人，培築高厚，無必不可措力之理。

translations.literal: Third, building dikes at Majia Bridge makes taking earth from Weishan inconvenient, and there is fear that throwing fascines at the water mouth will not hold firm—yet if the right men are entrusted, banks raised high and thick, there is no reason effort cannot be applied.
translations.idiomatic: Third, building dikes at Majia Bridge makes hauling earth from Weishan awkward, and fascines at the outlet may not hold—but with capable men in charge and banks built high and thick, there is no obstacle that effort cannot overcome.

sentences.zh: 開新河便。」

translations.literal: Opening the new channel is advantageous."
translations.idiomatic: Opening the new channel is the better course."

sentences.zh: 下廷臣集議，言新河已有次第，不可止。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to court ministers for joint deliberation; they said the new channel already had progress and must not be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The case went to a joint ministerial review, which found the new channel already well underway and argued it must not be halted.

sentences.zh: 況百中橋至留城白洋淺，出境山，疏浚補築，亦不全棄舊河，羣議俱合。

translations.literal: Moreover from Baizhong Bridge to Baiyang at Liucheng is shallow; leaving Jingshan, dredging and repair would not wholly abandon the old channel—all opinions agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the stretch from Baizhong Bridge to Baiyang at Liucheng was shallow; beyond Jingshan, dredging and repair would preserve parts of the old channel, and all sides agreed.

sentences.zh: 帝意乃決。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was then decided.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made up his mind.

sentences.zh: 時大雨，黃水驟發，決馬家橋，壞新築東西二堤。

translations.literal: At that time heavy rain fell, Yellow River water surged suddenly, breached Majia Bridge, and destroyed the newly built eastern and western dikes.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rains then sent the Yellow River surging; it broke through at Majia Bridge and destroyed the newly built eastern and western dikes.

sentences.zh: 給事中王元春、御史黃襄皆劾衡欺誤，起鳴亦變其說。

translations.literal: Censors Wang Yuanchun and Huang Xiang both impeached Heng for deception and error; Qiming also changed his view.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Wang Yuanchun and Huang Xiang both impeached Zhu Heng for misleading the court, and He Qiming reversed his position as well.

sentences.zh: 會衡奏新舊河百九十四里俱已流通，漕船至南陽出口無滯。

translations.literal: Just then Heng memorialized that old and new channels alike, one hundred ninety-four li, were already open; grain boats reached Nanyang's outlet without delay.
translations.idiomatic: At that point Zhu Heng reported that both old and new channels—one hundred ninety-four li in all—were open, and grain boats passed Nanyang's outlet without delay.

sentences.zh: 詔留衡與季馴詳議開上源、築長堤之便。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Heng and Jixun to deliberate in detail the advantage of opening the upper source and building long dikes.
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed Zhu Heng and Pan Jixun to study in detail the merits of opening the upper reaches and building long dikes.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年正月，衡請罷上源議，惟開廣秦溝，堅築南長堤。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Longqing, Heng asked to abandon the proposal to open the upper source and to open only Guangqin Ditch while firmly building the long southern dike.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Longqing 1, Zhu Heng asked to abandon the plan to open the upper reaches and to open only Guangqin Ditch while firmly building the long southern dike.

sentences.zh: 五月，新河成，西去舊河三十里。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the new channel was completed, thirty li west of the old river.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the new channel was completed, thirty li west of the old river.

sentences.zh: 舊河自留城以北，經謝溝、下沽頭、中沽頭、金溝四閘，過沛縣，又經廟道口、湖陵城、孟陽、八里灣、穀亭五閘，而至南陽閘。

translations.literal: The old river from north of Liucheng passed through four sluices—Xiegou, Xiagutou, Zhonggutou, and Jingou—crossed Pei County, and then through five more sluices—Miaodaokou, Hulingcheng, Mengyang, Balizhuan, and Guting—reaching Nanyang Sluice.
translations.idiomatic: The old river from north of Liucheng passed through four sluices—Xiegou, Xiagutou, Zhonggutou, and Jingou—crossed Pei County, and then through five more sluices—Miaodaokou, Hulingcheng, Mengyang, Balizhuan, and Guting—reaching Nanyang Sluice.

sentences.zh: 新河自留城而北，經馬家橋、西柳莊、滿家橋、夏鎮、楊莊、鵜硃梅、利建七閘，至南陽閘合舊河，凡百四十里有奇。

translations.literal: The new river from north of Liucheng passed through seven sluices—Majiaqiao, Xiliuzhuang, Manjiaqiao, Xiazhen, Yangzhuang, Tizhumei, and Lijian—joining the old river at Nanyang Sluice; altogether it ran a little more than one hundred forty li.
translations.idiomatic: The new river from north of Liucheng passed through seven sluices—Majiaqiao, Xiliuzhuang, Manjiaqiao, Xiazhen, Yangzhuang, Tizhumei, and Lijian—joining the old river at Nanyang Sluice; altogether it ran a little more than one hundred forty li.

sentences.zh: 又引鯰魚諸泉及薛河、沙河注其中，而設壩於三河之口，築馬家橋堤，遏黃水入秦溝，運道乃大通。

translations.literal: It also drew in the springs at Nianyu and diverted the Xue and Sha rivers into it; a dam was set at Sanhekou and a dike built at Majiaqiao to block Yellow River water from entering Qin Ditch, and the transport route then ran fully clear.
translations.idiomatic: It also drew in the Nianyu springs and diverted the Xue and Sha rivers into the channel; a dam was set at Sanhekou and a dike built at Majiaqiao to block Yellow River water from entering Qin Ditch, and the transport route then ran fully clear.

sentences.zh: 未幾，鯰魚口山水暴決，沒漕艘。

translations.literal: Before long mountain floods burst out at Nianyukou and submerged grain-transport boats.
translations.idiomatic: Before long mountain floods burst out at Nianyukou and submerged grain-transport boats.

sentences.zh: 帝從衡請，自東邵開支河三道以分泄之，又開支河於東邵之上，曆東滄橋以達百中橋，鑿豸裏溝諸處為渠，使水入赤山湖，由之以歸呂孟湖，下境山而去。

translations.literal: The emperor granted Heng's request: three branch channels were opened east from Dongshao to divide and discharge the water; branch channels were also opened above Dongshao, passing Dongcang Bridge to reach Baizhong Bridge, channels were cut at Zhili Gou and other places, sending water into Chishan Lake, from which it returned to Lü-Meng Lake and flowed down past Jingshan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted Zhu Heng's request: three branch channels were opened east from Dongshao to divide and discharge the water; branch channels were also opened above Dongshao, passing Dongcang Bridge to reach Baizhong Bridge, channels were cut at Zhili Gou and other places, sending water into Chishan Lake, from which it returned to Lü-Meng Lake and flowed down past Jingshan.

sentences.zh: 衡召入為工部尚書，都御史翁大立代，上言：「漕河資泉水，而地形東高西下，非湖瀦之則涸，故漕河以東皆有櫃；

translations.literal: Heng was summoned to the capital as Works Minister; Censor-in-Chief Weng Dali replaced him and memorialized: "The grain canal relies on spring water, yet the terrain runs high in the east and low in the west—without lakes to impound it, it dries; therefore east of the canal there are reservoirs;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Heng was recalled to serve as Works Minister, and Censor-in-Chief Weng Dali took his place, reporting: "The canal depends on spring water, but the land slopes down from east to west—without lakes to hold it, the channel runs dry, which is why there are reservoirs east of the canal;

sentences.zh: 非湖泄之則潰，故漕河以西皆有壑。

translations.literal: without lakes to discharge it, it bursts; therefore west of the canal there are spill basins.
translations.idiomatic: without lakes to release it, the banks burst, which is why there are spill basins west of the canal.

sentences.zh: 黃流逆奔，則以昭陽湖為散漫之區；

translations.literal: When the Yellow current rushes against the flow, Zhaoyang Lake serves as a zone of dispersion;
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River surges upstream, Zhaoyang Lake serves as a flood plain;

sentences.zh: 山水東突，則以南陽湖為瀦蓄之地。

translations.literal: when mountain waters burst eastward, Nanyang Lake serves as a place of impoundment.
translations.idiomatic: when mountain floods push eastward, Nanyang Lake serves as a storage basin.

sentences.zh: 宜由回回墓開通以達鴻溝，令穀亭、湖陵之水皆入昭陽湖，即浚鴻溝廢渠，引昭陽湖水沿渠東出留城。

translations.literal: It is fitting to open passage from Huihui Tomb to reach Honggou, let the waters of Guting and Huling all enter Zhaoyang Lake, then dredge Honggou's abandoned channel and lead Zhaoyang Lake water east along the channel out at Liucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Passage should be opened from Huihui Tomb to Honggou so the waters of Guting and Huling can all flow into Zhaoyang Lake; then Honggou's abandoned channel should be dredged to carry Zhaoyang Lake water east to Liucheng.

sentences.zh: 其湖地退灘者，又可得田數千頃。」

translations.literal: Where lake land receded to exposed flats, several thousand qing of fields could also be gained."
translations.idiomatic: Reclaimed lake flats could also yield several thousand qing of farmland."

sentences.zh: 大立又言：「薛河水湍悍，今盡注赤山湖，入微山湖以達呂孟湖，此尚書衡成績也。

translations.literal: Dali also said: "The Xue River runs swift and fierce; today it all pours into Chishan Lake, enters Weishan Lake to reach Lü-Meng Lake—this was Minister Heng's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Weng Dali added: "The Xue River runs swift and fierce; it now flows entirely into Chishan Lake, through Weishan Lake to Lü-Meng Lake—this was Minister Zhu Heng's achievement.

sentences.zh: 惟呂孟之南為邵家嶺，黃流填淤，地形高仰，秋水時至，翕納者小，浸淫平野，奪民田之利。

translations.literal: Only south of Lü-Meng is Shaojia Ridge; Yellow River flow fills and silts it, the terrain rises high, autumn water comes seasonally, intake capacity is small, and water spreads across the plain, seizing the people's fields.
translations.idiomatic: But south of Lü-Meng lies Shaojia Ridge, where Yellow River silt has raised the ground; when autumn floods arrive, the inlet can take only so much, and water spreads across the plain, ruining farmland.

sentences.zh: 微山之西為馬家橋，比草創一堤以開運道，土未及堅而時為積水所撼，以尋丈之址，二流夾攻，慮有傾圮。

translations.literal: West of Weishan is Majia Bridge; a dikes was hastily first built to open the transport route—the earth had not yet hardened when pooled water repeatedly undermined it; with a foundation only a few chi high, two currents attack from both sides, and collapse is feared.
translations.idiomatic: West of Weishan lies Majia Bridge, where a dikes was hurriedly thrown up to open transport—the earth had not yet set when standing water kept undermining it; with only a few chi of foundation, two currents press from both sides, and collapse is a real danger.

sentences.zh: 宜鑿邵家嶺，令水由地浜溝出境山以入漕河，則湖地可耕，河堤不潰。

translations.literal: Shaojia Ridge should be cut so water passes through Dibin Ditch out at Jingshan into the grain canal—then lake land can be farmed and river dikes will not burst.
translations.idiomatic: Shaojia Ridge should be cut so water can pass through Dibin Ditch at Jingshan into the canal; lake land could then be farmed and the dikes would hold.

sentences.zh: 更於馬家橋建減水閘，視旱澇為啟閉，乃通漕長策也。」

translations.literal: Further, build a flood-relief sluice at Majia Bridge, opening and closing according to drought and flood—this is the long-term plan for opening transport."
translations.idiomatic: A flood-relief sluice should also be built at Majia Bridge, opened or closed according to drought and flood—a lasting solution for keeping transport open."

sentences.zh: 並從之。

translations.literal: All was approved.
translations.idiomatic: All of these proposals were approved.

sentences.zh: 三年七月，河決沛縣，茶城淤塞，糧艘二千餘皆阻邳州。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year the river breached at Pei County; Chacheng silted shut, and more than two thousand grain boats were all blocked at Pizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Wanli 3 the river broke through at Pei County; Chacheng silted shut, and more than two thousand grain boats were stranded at Pizhou.

sentences.zh: 大立言：「臣按行徐州，循子房山，過梁山，至境山，入地浜溝，直趨馬家橋，上下八十里間，可別開一河以漕。」

translations.literal: Dali said: "Your servant inspected Xuzhou, followed Zifang Mountain, passed Liangshan, reached Jingshan, entered Dibin Ditch, and went straight toward Majia Bridge—within eighty li upstream and downstream a separate channel could be opened for transport."
translations.idiomatic: Weng Dali reported: "On inspection at Xuzhou I followed Zifang Mountain, passed Liangshan, reached Jingshan, and entered Dibin Ditch, running straight toward Majia Bridge; within eighty li upstream and downstream a separate canal could be cut for transport."

sentences.zh: 即所謂泇河也。

translations.literal: This is what is called the Jia River.
translations.idiomatic: This was the route known as the Jia River.

sentences.zh: 請集廷議，上即命行之。

translations.literal: He asked that court deliberation be convened; the emperor immediately ordered it carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for a court conference, and the emperor immediately ordered the plan put into effect.

sentences.zh: 未幾，黃落漕通，前議遂寢。

translations.literal: Before long the Yellow River subsided and transport reopened; the earlier proposal was then shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Yellow River fell and transport resumed, and the earlier proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 時淮水漲溢，自清河至淮安城西淤三十餘里，決禮、信二壩出海，寶應湖堤多壞。

translations.literal: At that time Huai water rose and overflowed; from Qinghe to west of Huai'an city more than thirty li silted up, the Li and Xin dams were breached to reach the sea, and many dikes on Lake Baoying were damaged.
translations.idiomatic: The Huai then rose and overflowed; from Qinghe to west of Huai'an city more than thirty li silted up, the Li and Xin dams were cut to discharge to the sea, and many dikes on Lake Baoying were breached.

sentences.zh: 山東諸水從直河出邳州。

translations.literal: Shandong's various waters exited at Pizhou through the Straight River.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong's waters were all draining to Pizhou through the Straight River.

sentences.zh: 大立以聞。

translations.literal: Dali reported this.
translations.idiomatic: Weng Dali reported the situation to the throne.

sentences.zh: 其冬，自淮安板閘至清河西湖嘴開浚垂成，而裏口復塞。

translations.literal: That winter, dredging from Huai'an's Ban Sluice to Xihuzui at Qinghe was nearly finished, but the inner mouth silted shut again.
translations.idiomatic: That winter dredging from Huai'an's Ban Sluice to Xihuzui at Qinghe was nearly complete, but the inner mouth silted shut again.

sentences.zh: 督漕侍郎趙孔昭言：「清江一帶黃河五十里，宜築堰以防河溢；

translations.literal: Grain Transport Vice-Minister Zhao Kongzhao said: "Along the Qingjiang stretch the Yellow River runs fifty li—a dam should be built to guard against river overflow;
translations.idiomatic: Grain Transport Vice-Minister Zhao Kongzhao proposed: "Along the fifty-li Qingjiang reach of the Yellow River, a dam should be built to hold back floods;

sentences.zh: 淮河高良澗一帶七十餘里，宜築堰以防淮漲。」

translations.literal: along the Huai River's Gaoliangjian stretch for more than seventy li, a dam should be built to guard against Huai flooding."
translations.idiomatic: along the seventy-plus li of the Huai at Gaoliangjian, a dam should be built to hold back rising Huai water."

sentences.zh: 帝令亟浚裏口，與大立商築堰事宜，並議海口築塞及寶應月河二事。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the inner mouth dredged urgently, discussed dam construction with Dali, and also deliberated blocking the river mouth and the Baoying bypass channel.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the inner mouth dredged at once, told Weng Dali to plan the dams, and also took up sealing the river mouth and the Baoying bypass channel.

sentences.zh: 四年六月，淮河及鴻溝境山疏浚工竣。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year dredging of the Huai River and Honggou at Jingshan was completed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Wanli 4 dredging of the Huai River and Honggou at Jingshan was finished.

sentences.zh: 大立方奏聞，諸水忽驟溢，決仲家淺，與黃河合，茶城復淤。

translations.literal: Dali had just memorialized when all the waters suddenly surged, breached Zhongjia Shoal, joined the Yellow River, and Chacheng silted shut again.
translations.idiomatic: Weng Dali had just reported completion when the waters surged, broke through at Zhongjia Shoal, merged with the Yellow River, and Chacheng silted shut again.

sentences.zh: 未幾，自泰山廟至七里溝，淮河淤十餘里，其水從硃家溝旁出，至清河縣河南鎮以合於黃河。

translations.literal: Before long, from Taishan Temple to Qiligou the Huai silted for more than ten li; its water exited beside Zhujia Ditch and reached Henanzhen in Qinghe County to join the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Huai silted up for more than ten li from Taishan Temple to Qiligou; its water spilled out through Zhujia Ditch and reached Henanzhen in Qinghe County, where it joined the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 大立請開新莊閘以通回船，兼浚古睢河，泄二洪水，且分河自魚溝下草灣，保南北運道。

translations.literal: Dali asked to open Xinzhuang Sluice for returning boats, dredge the ancient Sui River as well to discharge the two floods, and also divide the river from Yugou down to Caowan to protect the north-south transport route.
translations.idiomatic: Weng Dali proposed opening Xinzhuang Sluice for return traffic, dredging the old Sui River to spill the two flood streams, and splitting the river from Yugou down to Caowan to safeguard transport north and south.

sentences.zh: 帝命新任總河都御史潘季馴區畫。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the newly appointed Grand Canal Censor-in-Chief Pan Jixun to plan it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor put the newly appointed Grand Canal Censor-in-Chief Pan Jixun in charge of planning.

sentences.zh: 頃之，河大決邳州，睢寧運道淤百餘里。

translations.literal: Shortly after, the river breached greatly at Pizhou; the Suining transport route silted for more than one hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the river broke catastrophically at Pizhou, and the Suining transport route silted shut for more than one hundred li.

sentences.zh: 大立請開泇口、蕭縣二河。

translations.literal: Dali asked to open the Jia River mouth and the two channels at Xiao County.
translations.idiomatic: Weng Dali proposed opening the Jia River mouth and two channels at Xiao County.

sentences.zh: 會季馴築塞諸決，河水歸正流，漕船獲通。

translations.literal: Just then Jixun built and blocked the various breaches; river water returned to the main current and grain boats passed.
translations.idiomatic: By then Pan Jixun had sealed the breaches, the river returned to its main course, and grain boats got through.

sentences.zh: 大立、孔昭皆以遲誤漕糧削籍，開泇之議不果行。

translations.literal: Dali and Kongzhao were both struck from the register for delaying grain transport; the proposal to open the Jia River was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Weng Dali and Zhao Kongzhao were both dismissed from office for delaying grain transport, and the plan to open the Jia River was never implemented.

sentences.zh: 五年四月，河復決邳州王家口，自雙溝而下，南北決口十餘，損漕船運軍千計，沒糧四十萬餘石，而匙頭灣以下八十里皆淤。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifth year the river breached again at Wangjiakou in Pizhou; from Shuanggou downstream more than ten breaches north and south damaged on the order of a thousand grain boats and transport troops, drowned more than four hundred thousand shi of grain, and silted everything below Shitou Bay for eighty li.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Wanli 5 the river broke through again at Wangjiakou in Pizhou; from Shuanggou downstream there were more than ten breaches north and south, destroying roughly a thousand grain boats and transport troops, sinking more than four hundred thousand shi of grain, and silting the channel below Shitou Bay for eighty li.

sentences.zh: 於是膠、萊海運之議紛起。

translations.literal: Thereupon proposals for Jiao-Lai sea transport arose in profusion.
translations.idiomatic: Proposals for the Jiao-Lai sea route then proliferated.

sentences.zh: 會季馴奏邳河功成。

translations.literal: Just then Jixun memorialized that the Pizhou river works were completed.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Jixun then reported that the Pizhou river works were finished.

sentences.zh: 帝以漕運遲，遣給事中雒遵往勘。

translations.literal: Because grain transport was delayed, the emperor dispatched censor Luo Zun to survey.
translations.idiomatic: Because transport was running late, the emperor sent censor Luo Zun to inspect the situation.

sentences.zh: 總漕陳炌及季馴俱罷官。

translations.literal: Grand Grain Transport Supervisor Chen Can and Jixun were both dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Grain Transport Supervisor Chen Can and Pan Jixun were both removed from office.

sentences.zh: 六年，從雒遵言，修築茶城至清河長堤五百五十里，三里一鋪，鋪十夫，設官畫地而守。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, following Luo Zun's proposal, a long dike from Chacheng to Qinghe was built for five hundred fifty li, one depot every three li with ten laborers per depot, and officials assigned to demarcate and guard the ground.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 6, following Luo Zun's recommendation, a five-hundred-fifty-li long dike was built from Chacheng to Qinghe, with a maintenance station every three li staffed by ten men, and officials assigned to patrol defined sections.

sentences.zh: 又接築茶城至開封兩岸堤。

translations.literal: Dikes on both banks from Chacheng to Kaifeng were also joined and built.
translations.idiomatic: Dikes on both banks from Chacheng to Kaifeng were extended as well.

sentences.zh: 從硃衡言，繕豐、沛大黃堤。

translations.literal: Following Zhu Heng's words, repair the great Yellow River dikes at Feng and Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Following Zhu Heng's recommendation, the great Yellow River dikes at Feng and Pei were repaired.

sentences.zh: 衡又言：「漕河起儀真訖張家灣二千八百餘里，河勢凡四段，各不相同。

translations.literal: Heng also said: "The grain canal runs from Yizhen to Zhangjiawan for more than two thousand eight hundred li; the river's situation falls into four sections, each not the same.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Heng also reported: "The Grand Canal runs from Yizhen to Zhangjiawan—a distance of more than twenty-eight hundred li—and its conditions fall into four sections, no two alike.

sentences.zh: 清江浦以南，臨清以北，皆遠隔黃河，不煩用力。

translations.literal: South of Qingjiangpu and north of Linqing are all far separated from the Yellow River; no trouble need be taken.
translations.idiomatic: South of Qingjiangpu and north of Linqing lie far from the Yellow River and require little effort.

sentences.zh: 惟茶城至臨清，則閘諸泉為河，與黃相近。

translations.literal: Only from Chacheng to Linqing do sluiced springs form the river, close to the Yellow.
translations.idiomatic: Only from Chacheng to Linqing does a river formed by sluiced springs run close to the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 清河至茶城，則黃河即運河也。

translations.literal: From Qinghe to Chacheng, the Yellow River is the transport canal.
translations.idiomatic: From Qinghe to Chacheng, the Yellow River is the Grand Canal itself.

sentences.zh: 茶城以北，當防黃河之決而入；

translations.literal: North of Chacheng, one must guard against Yellow River breaches flowing in;
translations.idiomatic: North of Chacheng, one must guard against Yellow River breaches pouring in;

sentences.zh: 茶城以南，當防黃河之決而出。

translations.literal: South of Chacheng, one must guard against Yellow River breaches flowing out.
translations.idiomatic: south of Chacheng, one must guard against Yellow River breaches breaking out.

sentences.zh: 防黃河即所以保運河，故自茶城至邳、遷，高築兩堤，宿遷至清河，盡塞缺口，蓋以防黃水之出，則正河必淤，昨歲徐、邳之患是也。

translations.literal: Guarding the Yellow River is precisely how to protect the transport canal; therefore from Chacheng to Pi and Qian, two dikes were built high, and from Suqian to Qinghe all gaps were filled—this was to guard against Yellow water flowing out, for then the main channel would surely silt up, as was last year's disaster in Xu and Pi.
translations.idiomatic: Defending against the Yellow River is how one protects the canal; therefore from Chacheng to Pi and Qian, twin dikes were raised high, and from Suqian to Qinghe every breach was closed—meant to keep Yellow River water from breaking out, which would silt the main channel, as happened in the Xu-Pi disaster the year before.

sentences.zh: 自茶城秦溝口至豐、沛、曹、單，創築增築以接縷水舊堤，蓋以防黃水之入，則正河必決，往年曹、沛之患是也。

translations.literal: From Chacheng's Qingou Mouth to Feng, Pei, Cao, and Shan, new construction and additions were built to join the old Lüshui dikes—this was to guard against Yellow water flowing in, for then the main channel would surely breach, as was the disaster in Cao and Pei in years past.
translations.idiomatic: From Chacheng's Qingou Mouth through Feng, Pei, Cao, and Shan, new and extended dikes were built to connect with the old Lüshui embankments—meant to keep Yellow River water from breaking in, which would burst the main channel, as had happened in Cao and Pei in earlier years.

sentences.zh: 二處告竣，故河深水束，無旁決中潰之虞。

translations.literal: Both places reported completion; therefore the river ran deep and the water was confined, with no fear of breach from the sides or collapse in the middle.
translations.idiomatic: With both sections finished, the river ran deep and the water was confined, and there was no longer fear of lateral breaches or collapse in the channel bed.

sentences.zh: 沛縣之窯子頭至秦溝口，應築堤七十里，接古北堤。

translations.literal: From Yaozitou in Pei County to Qingou Mouth, seventy li of dikes should be built, joining the ancient northern dike.
translations.idiomatic: From Yaozitou in Pei County to Qingou Mouth, seventy li of dikes should be built to connect with the ancient northern embankment.

sentences.zh: 徐、邳之間，堤逼河身，宜於新堤外別築遙堤。」

translations.literal: Between Xu and Pi, the dikes press close to the river channel; it is fitting to build separate distant dikes outside the new dikes."
translations.idiomatic: Between Xu and Pi the dikes hugged the riverbed too closely; separate outer dikes should be built beyond the new embankments."

sentences.zh: 詔如其議，以命總河侍郎萬恭。

translations.literal: An edict approved his proposal and appointed Grand Canal Vice-Minister Wan Gong to carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the plan and put Grand Canal Vice-Minister Wan Gong in charge.

sentences.zh: 萬曆元年，恭言：「祖宗時造淺船近萬，非不知滿載省舟之便，以閘河流淺，故不敢過四百石也。

translations.literal: In Wanli 1, Gong said: "In the forefathers' time nearly ten thousand shallow-draft boats were built—not because they did not know the convenience of full loads and fewer boats, but because the sluice river was shallow, so they dared not exceed four hundred shi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wanli, Wan Gong reported: "Our forebears built nearly ten thousand shallow-draft boats—not because they failed to see the advantage of full loads and fewer vessels, but because the sluice river was shallow, and they dared not exceed four hundred shi per boat.

sentences.zh: 其制底平、倉淺，底平則入水不深，倉淺則負載不滿。

translations.literal: Their design had flat bottoms and shallow holds: flat bottoms mean less draft, shallow holds mean less cargo.
translations.idiomatic: They were built with flat bottoms and shallow holds—flat bottoms kept draft shallow, and shallow holds kept cargo light.

sentences.zh: 又限淺船用水不得過六拏，伸大指與食指相距為一拏，六拏不過三尺許，明受水淺也。

translations.literal: Shallow boats were also limited to draft of no more than six na—the span between extended thumb and forefinger being one na; six na came to about three chi, showing how shallow their draft was.
translations.idiomatic: Shallow boats were also limited to a draft of no more than six na—a na being the span between thumb and forefinger; six na came to about three chi, a clear sign of how shallow their draft was meant to be.

sentences.zh: 今不務遵行，而競僱船搭運。

translations.literal: Now people do not seek to follow this, but compete to hire boats for relay transport.
translations.idiomatic: Today the old rules are ignored, and officials compete to hire boats for relay transport instead.

sentences.zh: 僱船有三害，搭運有五害，皆病河道。

translations.literal: Hiring boats has three harms; relay transport has five harms—all afflict the canal.
translations.idiomatic: Hiring boats brings three evils, and relay transport five—all of them harmful to the canal.

sentences.zh: 請悉遵舊制。」

translations.literal: I ask that the old system be fully followed."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the old system be fully restored."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: His request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 恭又請復淮南平水諸閘，上言：「高、寶諸湖周遭數百里，西受天長七十餘河，徒恃百里長堤，若障之使無疏泄，是潰堤也。

translations.literal: Gong also asked to restore the level-water sluices south of the Huai, memorializing: "The lakes of Gaoyou and Baoying extend several hundred li around; from the west they receive more than seventy rivers from Tianchang. To rely solely on a hundred-li long dike and block them with no outlet is to burst the dikes.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Gong also asked to restore the level-water sluices south of the Huai, reporting: "The Gaoyou and Baoying lakes stretch for hundreds of li; from the west they take in more than seventy rivers from Tianchang. To rely on a hundred-li long dike alone and block them with no outlet is to burst the dikes.

sentences.zh: 以故祖宗之法，偏置數十小閘於長堤之間，又為令曰：「但許深湖，不許高堤」，故設淺船淺夫取湖之淤以厚堤。

translations.literal: For this reason the forefathers' method placed dozens of small sluices along the long dike, and issued an order: "Only deepen the lakes, do not raise the dikes"—hence shallow boats and shallow-draft laborers were assigned to take silt from the lakes to thicken the dikes.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the forefathers placed dozens of small sluices along the long dike and issued the rule: "Deepen the lakes, do not raise the dikes"—and why shallow boats and dredging crews were assigned to take lake silt to thicken the embankments.

sentences.zh: 夫閘多則水易落而堤堅，浚勤則湖愈深而堤厚，意至深遠也。

translations.literal: Many sluices mean water falls easily and dikes stand firm; diligent dredging means lakes grow deeper and dikes thicker—the design runs very deep.
translations.idiomatic: Many sluices let water fall easily and keep dikes firm; steady dredging deepens the lakes and thickens the dikes—the intent was far-sighted indeed.

sentences.zh: 比年畏修閘之勞，每壞一閘即堙一閘，歲月既久，諸閘盡堙，而長堤為死障矣。

translations.literal: In recent years, fearing the labor of repairing sluices, whenever one broke they simply filled it in; over time all the sluices were buried, and the long dike became a dead barrier.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years, dreading the labor of repairing sluices, officials filled in every sluice that failed; in time all the sluices were buried, and the long dike became a dead wall.

sentences.zh: 畏浚淺之苦，每湖淺一尺則加堤一尺，歲月既久，湖水捧起，而高、寶為盂城矣。

translations.literal: Fearing the hardship of dredging shallows, for every chi the lake shoaled they raised the dike a chi; over time lake water was held up, and Gaoyou and Baoying became basin cities.
translations.idiomatic: Dreading the toil of dredging, they raised the dikes a chi for every chi the lakes shoaled; over the years the lake water was lifted higher and higher, until Gaoyou and Baoying stood like cities in a bowl.

sentences.zh: 且湖漕勿堤與無漕同，湖堤勿閘與無堤同。

translations.literal: Moreover, lake transport without dikes is the same as no transport; lake dikes without sluices are the same as no dikes.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, lake transport without dikes is no transport at all, and lake dikes without sluices are no dikes at all.

sentences.zh: 陳瑄大置減水閘數十，湖水溢則瀉以利堤，水落則閉以利漕，最為完計。

translations.literal: Chen Xuan greatly placed dozens of flood-discharge sluices; when lake water overflowed they drained to benefit the dikes, when water fell they closed to benefit transport—the most complete plan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xuan installed dozens of flood-discharge sluices: when the lakes rose, water was released to protect the dikes; when they fell, the sluices closed to aid transport—it was the soundest design of all.

sentences.zh: 積久而減水故跡不可復得，湖且沉堤。

translations.literal: Over long accumulation the old traces of flood discharge could no longer be recovered, and the lakes were sinking the dikes.
translations.idiomatic: Over time the old flood-discharge works could no longer be found, and the lakes began to swallow the dikes.

sentences.zh: 請復建平水閘，閘欲密，密則水疏，無漲懣患；

translations.literal: I ask to restore and build level-water sluices; sluices should be dense—dense, then water drains, with no flooding and stagnation trouble;
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the level-water sluices be rebuilt: they should be closely spaced—close spacing drains water and prevents flooding and stagnation;

sentences.zh: 閘欲狹，狹則勢緩，無齧決虞。」

translations.literal: sluices should be narrow—narrow, then the force is gentle, with no fear of erosion and breach."
translations.idiomatic: and they should be narrow—narrow channels slow the current and prevent erosion and breach."

sentences.zh: 尚書衡覆奏如其請。

translations.literal: Minister Heng memorialized in reply approving his request.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zhu Heng submitted a follow-up memorial endorsing the request.

sentences.zh: 於是儀直、江都、高郵、寶應、山陽設閘二十三，浚淺凡五十一處，各設撈淺船二，淺夫十。

translations.literal: Thereupon twenty-three sluices were set at Yizhi, Jiangdu, Gaoyou, Baoying, and Shanyang; dredging of shallows totaled fifty-one places, each with two shallow-dredging boats and ten shallow-draft laborers.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-three sluices were then established at Yizhi, Jiangdu, Gaoyou, Baoying, and Shanyang; fifty-one shallow sections were dredged, each with two dredging boats and ten dredging crews.

sentences.zh: 恭又言：「清江浦河六十里，陳瑄浚至天妃祠東，注於黃河。

translations.literal: Gong also said: "The Qingjiangpu River runs sixty li; Chen Xuan dredged it east to Tianfei Shrine, where it emptied into the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Gong also reported: "The Qingjiangpu channel runs sixty li; Chen Xuan dredged it east to Tianfei Shrine, where it joined the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 運艘出天妃口入黃穿清特半餉耳。

translations.literal: Transport vessels leaving Tianfei Mouth entered the Yellow, crossed the clear channel—only half a day's grain ration.
translations.idiomatic: Grain boats leaving Tianfei Mouth entered the Yellow River and crossed the clear channel in only half a day's travel.

sentences.zh: 後黃漲，逆注入口，清遂多淤。

translations.literal: Later the Yellow rose and flowed back into the mouth; the clear channel then silted heavily.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Yellow River rose, it backed into the mouth and the clear channel silted badly.

sentences.zh: 議者不制天妃口而遽塞之，令淮水勿與黃值。

translations.literal: Those debating did not control Tianfei Mouth but hastily blocked it, ordering Huai water not to meet the Yellow.
translations.idiomatic: Planners did not regulate Tianfei Mouth but hurriedly blocked it, so Huai water would not meet the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 開新河以接淮河，曰：「接清流勿接濁流，可不淤也」。

translations.literal: They opened a new river to join the Huai River, saying: "Join clear flow, do not join muddy flow—then it will not silt."
translations.idiomatic: They cut a new channel to link with the Huai, saying: "Connect clear water, not muddy water, and it will not silt up."

sentences.zh: 不知黃河非安流之水，伏秋盛發，則西擁淮流數十里，並灌新開河。

translations.literal: They did not know the Yellow River is not a tranquil flow; in the hidden-flood and autumn season when it surges, it pushes the Huai current west for dozens of li and floods the newly opened river together.
translations.idiomatic: They failed to see that the Yellow River is no gentle stream: in the flood season it surges west for dozens of li, pushing the Huai before it and pouring into the new channel.

sentences.zh: 彼天妃口，一黃水之淤耳。

translations.literal: That Tianfei Mouth was only one Yellow-water silting.
translations.idiomatic: At Tianfei Mouth there was only one source of Yellow River silt.

sentences.zh: 今淮、黃會於新閘開河口，是二淤也。

translations.literal: Now Huai and Yellow meet at the new sluice's river mouth—this is two siltings.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Huai and Yellow meet at the new sluice's outlet—two sources of silt instead of one.

sentences.zh: 防一淤，生二淤，又生淮、黃交會之淺。

translations.literal: Guarding one silting produced two siltings, and also produced the shallows where Huai and Yellow meet.
translations.idiomatic: Blocking one silting point created two, and also created the shallow junction where the Huai and Yellow meet.

sentences.zh: 歲役丁夫千百，浚治方畢，水過復合。

translations.literal: Each year thousands of laborers were conscripted; dredging was just finished when water passed and silted again.
translations.idiomatic: Every year thousands of laborers were drafted; dredging was barely finished before the waters rose and silted the channel again.

sentences.zh: 又使運艘迂八里淺滯而始達於清河，孰與出天妃口者之便且利？

translations.literal: Moreover, transport vessels were made to detour eight li of shallow sluggish water before reaching Qinghe—how does that compare with leaving Tianfei Mouth for convenience and profit?
translations.idiomatic: Grain boats were forced to wind eight li through shallow, sluggish water before reaching Qinghe—how can that match the ease and efficiency of the Tianfei Mouth route?

sentences.zh: 請建天妃閘，俾漕船直達清河。

translations.literal: I ask to build a Tianfei sluice so grain boats can reach Qinghe directly.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that a Tianfei sluice be built so grain boats can reach Qinghe directly.

sentences.zh: 運盡而黃水盛發，則閉閘絕黃，水落則啟天妃閘以利商船。

translations.literal: When transport was finished and Yellow water surged, close the sluice to cut off the Yellow; when water fell, open Tianfei sluice to benefit merchant boats.
translations.idiomatic: When transport was complete and the Yellow River rose, the sluice would close to shut out muddy water; when the river fell, Tianfei sluice would open to let merchant boats through.

sentences.zh: 新河口勿浚可也。」。

translations.literal: The new river mouth need not be dredged."
translations.idiomatic: The new outlet need not be dredged at all."

sentences.zh: 乃建天妃廟口石閘。

translations.literal: Thereupon a stone sluice was built at Tianfei Temple Mouth.
translations.idiomatic: A stone sluice was then built at Tianfei Temple Mouth.

sentences.zh: 恭又言：「由黃河入閘河為茶城，出臨清板閘七百餘里，舊有七十二淺。

translations.literal: Gong also said: "From entering the sluice river at the Yellow River at Chacheng to leaving Linqing's Ban sluice is more than seven hundred li; formerly there were seventy-two shallows.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Gong also reported: "From Chacheng, where the canal leaves the Yellow River, to the Ban sluice at Linqing is more than seven hundred li; there were once seventy-two shallow sections.

sentences.zh: 自創開新河，汶流平衍，地勢高下不甚相懸，七十淺悉為通渠。

translations.literal: Since the new river was first opened, the Wen flow spread level; terrain high and low did not differ greatly, and seventy shallows all became open channels.
translations.idiomatic: After the new channel was cut, the Wen River spread evenly and the land rose and fell only gently; seventy shallows became open passage.

sentences.zh: 惟茶、黃交會間，運盛之時，正值黃河水落之候，高下不相接，是以有茶城黃家閘之淺，連年患之。

translations.literal: Only at the junction of Chacheng and the Yellow, when transport was at its peak, it coincided with the Yellow River's falling season; high and low did not connect—hence the shallow at Chacheng's Huangjia sluice, a trouble year after year.
translations.idiomatic: Only at the Chacheng-Yellow River junction, when transport peaked, the Yellow River was at its low stage and the levels did not meet—hence the chronic shallow at Huangjia sluice near Chacheng, a problem year after year.

sentences.zh: 祖宗時，嘗建境山閘，自新河水平，閘沒泥淖且丈餘。

translations.literal: In the forefathers' time Jingshan sluice was once built; since the new river ran level, the sluice was buried in mud more than a zhang deep.
translations.idiomatic: In the forefathers' time Jingshan sluice had been built, but once the new channel leveled out, the sluice sank more than a zhang deep in mud.

sentences.zh: 其閘上距黃家閘二十里，下接茶城十里，因故基累石為之，可留黃家閘外二十里之上流，接茶城內十里之下流，且挾二十里水勢，沖十里之狹流，蔑不勝矣。」

translations.literal: Above the sluice it was twenty li from Huangjia sluice; below it joined Chacheng for ten li. Rebuilding on the old foundation with piled stone, it could hold twenty li of upstream above Huangjia sluice and join ten li of downstream within Chacheng—and with twenty li of water force, rush the ten-li narrow flow: nothing could fail to be overcome."
translations.idiomatic: The sluice stood twenty li above Huangjia sluice and ten li below Chacheng; rebuilt on the old foundation with stone, it could hold twenty li of upstream above Huangjia sluice and feed ten li of downstream within Chacheng—carrying twenty li of head to drive through ten li of narrow channel, nothing could fail to yield."

sentences.zh: 乃復境山舊閘。

translations.literal: Thereupon the old Jingshan sluice was restored.
translations.idiomatic: The old Jingshan sluice was then restored.

sentences.zh: 恭建三議，尚書衡覆行之，為運道永利。

translations.literal: Gong's three proposals were reviewed and carried out by Minister Heng, bringing lasting benefit to the transport route.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Gong's three proposals were reviewed and implemented by Minister Zhu Heng, securing lasting benefit for the transport route.

sentences.zh: 而是時，茶城歲淤，恭方報正河安流，回空船速出。

translations.literal: But at this time Chacheng silted yearly; Gong had just reported the main channel flowed safely and empty return boats passed quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at that very time Chacheng was silting every year, even as Wan Gong reported that the main channel ran clear and empty return boats were moving swiftly.

sentences.zh: 給事中硃南雍以回空多阻，劾恭隱蔽溺職。

translations.literal: Censor Zhu Nanyong, because empty returns were often blocked, impeached Gong for concealment and neglect of duty.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhu Nanyong impeached Wan Gong for concealing the truth and neglecting his duties, citing the frequent delays to empty return boats.

sentences.zh: 帝切責恭，罷去。

translations.literal: The emperor sharply rebuked Gong and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sharply rebuked Wan Gong and removed him from office.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，總河都御史傅希摯請開泇河以避黃險，不果行。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year, Grand Canal Censor-in-Chief Fu Xizhi asked to open the Jia River to avoid Yellow River danger; it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Wanli 3, Grand Canal Censor-in-Chief Fu Xizhi proposed opening the Jia River to bypass Yellow River hazards, but the plan was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 希摯又請浚梁山以下，與茶城互用，淤舊則通新而挑舊，淤新則通舊而挑新，築壩斷流，常通其一以備不虞。

translations.literal: Xizhi also asked to dredge below Liangshan and use it alternately with Chacheng: if the old silted, open the new and dredge the old; if the new silted, open the old and dredge the new—build dams to cut flow and always keep one open against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xizhi also proposed dredging below Liangshan and alternating it with Chacheng: when the old route silted, open the new and dredge the old; when the new silted, open the old and dredge the new—building dams to cut the flow and always keeping one route open as a safeguard.

sentences.zh: 詔從所請。

translations.literal: An edict approved his request.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 工未成，而河決崔鎮，淮決高家堰，高郵湖決清水潭、丁志等口，淮城幾沒。

translations.literal: The work was not finished when the river breached at Cuizhen, the Huai breached at Gaojiayan, Gaoyou Lake breached at Qingshuitan, Dingzhi, and other mouths, and Huai'an city nearly drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Before the work was finished, the river broke through at Cuizhen, the Huai broke at Gaojiayan, Gaoyou Lake broke at Qingshuitan, Dingzhi, and other points, and Huai'an city nearly went under.

sentences.zh: 知府邵元哲開菊花潭，以泄淮安、高、寶三城之水，東方芻米少通。

translations.literal: Prefect Shao Yuanzhe opened Juhua Tan to drain the waters of Huai'an, Gaoyou, and Baoying—the three cities—and fodder and grain in the east barely got through.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Shao Yuanzhe opened Juhua Tan to drain Huai'an, Gaoyou, and Baoying, and fodder and grain from the east began to move again, if only barely.

sentences.zh: 明年春，督漕侍郎張翀以築清水潭堤工鉅不克就，欲令糧船暫由圈子田以行。

translations.literal: The next spring, Grain Transport Vice-Minister Zhang Chong, because the Qingshuitan dike works were huge and could not be completed, wished to have grain boats temporarily travel by Quanzitian.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring, Grain Transport Vice-Minister Zhang Chong, finding the Qingshuitan dike project too vast to finish, proposed routing grain boats temporarily through Quanzitian.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史陳功不可。

translations.literal: Investigating Censor Chen Gong would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censor Chen Gong refused.

sentences.zh: 河漕侍郎吳桂芳言：「高郵湖老堤，陳瑄所建。

translations.literal: Canal Vice-Minister Wu Guifang said: "Gaoyou Lake's old dike was built by Chen Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Canal Vice-Minister Wu Guifang reported: "Gaoyou Lake's old dike was built by Chen Xuan.

sentences.zh: 後白昂開月河，距湖數里，中為土堤，東為石堤，首尾建閘，名為康濟河。

translations.literal: Later Bai Ang opened a moon river several li from the lake; in the middle was an earthen dike, to the east a stone dike, with sluices at both ends—named Kangji River.
translations.idiomatic: Later Bai Ang cut a moon river several li from the lake, with an earthen dike in the middle and a stone dike to the east, sluices at both ends, and called it the Kangji River.

sentences.zh: 其中堤之西，老堤之東，民田數萬畝，所謂圈子田也。

translations.literal: West of the middle dike and east of the old dike lay tens of thousands of mu of civilian fields—the so-called Quanzitian.
translations.idiomatic: Between the middle dike to the west and the old dike to the east lay tens of thousands of mu of farmland—the so-called Quanzitian, the Encircled Fields.

sentences.zh: 河湖相去太遠，老堤缺壞不修，遂至水入圈田，又成一湖。

translations.literal: River and lake were too far apart; the old dike broke and was not repaired, until water entered Quanzitian and formed another lake.
translations.idiomatic: Because the river and lake stood too far apart, the old dike was left broken and unrepaired, until water poured into Quanzitian and formed a new lake.

sentences.zh: 而中堤潰壞，東堤獨受數百里湖濤，清水潭之決，勢所必至。

translations.literal: The middle dike collapsed; the eastern dike alone bore lake waves for hundreds of li—the breach at Qingshuitan was bound to come.
translations.idiomatic: When the middle dike failed, the eastern dike alone bore the lake surge for hundreds of li—the breach at Qingshuitan was inevitable.

sentences.zh: 宜遵弘治間王恕之議，就老堤為月河，但修東西二堤，費省而工易舉。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to follow Wang Shu's proposal from the Hongzhi era: make the old dike the moon river, and only repair the eastern and western dikes—cost saved and work easy to accomplish."
translations.idiomatic: We should follow Wang Shu's Hongzhi-era proposal: turn the old dike into the moon river and repair only the eastern and western dikes—saving expense and making the work easier."

sentences.zh: 帝命如所請行之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered it carried out as requested.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the plan implemented as proposed.

sentences.zh: 是年，元哲修築淮安長堤，又疏鹽城石鵜達口下流入海。

translations.literal: That year Yuanzhe repaired and built Huai'an's long dike, and also dredged Yancheng's Shijunda Mouth so its lower flow reached the sea.
translations.idiomatic: That year Shao Yuanzhe repaired Huai'an's long dike and dredged Yancheng's Shijunda outlet so its lower reach flowed to the sea.

sentences.zh: 五年二月，高郵石堤將成，桂芳請傍老堤十數丈開挑月河。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifth year, as Gaoyou's stone dike was nearing completion, Guifang asked to open and cut a moon river a dozen or so zhang beside the old dike.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Wanli 5, as Gaoyou's stone dike neared completion, Wu Guifang proposed cutting a moon river a dozen zhang or so beside the old dike.

sentences.zh: 因言：「白昂康濟月河去老堤太遠，人心狃月河之安，忘老堤外捍之力。

translations.literal: He added: "Bai Ang's Kangji moon river was too far from the old dike; people's minds grew accustomed to the moon river's safety and forgot the old dike's power to hold back from outside.
translations.idiomatic: He explained: "Bai Ang's Kangji moon river lay too far from the old dike; people grew complacent about the moon river's safety and forgot how much the old dike still held back the lake.

sentences.zh: 年復一年，不加省視，老、中二堤俱壞，而東堤不能獨存。

translations.literal: Year after year without inspection, the old and middle dikes both failed, and the eastern dike could not stand alone.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year without inspection, both the old and middle dikes failed, and the eastern dike could not stand alone.

sentences.zh: 今河與老堤近，則易於管攝。」

translations.literal: Now with the river close to the old dike, oversight is easy."
translations.idiomatic: With the channel close to the old dike, it will be easier to supervise."

sentences.zh: 御史陳世寶論江北河道，請於寶應湖堤補石堤以固其外，而於石堤之東復築一堤，以通月河，漕舟行其中。

translations.literal: Censor Chen Shibao, discussing Jiangbei canal routes, asked to add stone dikes to Baoying Lake's embankment to strengthen the outside, and east of the stone dike build another dike to carry the moon river, with grain boats traveling between them.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Chen Shibao, reviewing Jiangbei canal routes, proposed adding stone dikes to Baoying Lake's embankment to strengthen the outer face, and building another dike east of the stone dike to carry the moon river, with grain boats running between them.

sentences.zh: 並議行。

translations.literal: Both proposals were approved for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Both proposals were approved.

sentences.zh: 其冬，高郵湖土石二堤、新開漕河南北二閘及老堤加石、增護堤木城各工竣事。

translations.literal: That winter, Gaoyou Lake's earthen and stone dikes, the north and south sluices of the newly opened grain canal, stone facing added to the old dike, and timber crib revetments added to protect the dikes—all works were completed.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the earthen and stone dikes on Gaoyou Lake, the north and south sluices of the newly opened canal, the stone facing added to the old dike, and the timber crib revetments—all were finished.

sentences.zh: 桂芳又與元哲增築山陽長堤，自板閘至黃浦亙七十里，閉通濟閘不用，而建興文閘，且修新莊諸閘，築清江浦南堤，創板閘漕堤，南北與新舊堤接。

translations.literal: Guifang also joined Yuanzhe in extending Shanyang's long dike from Ban sluice to Huangpu for seventy li; Tongji sluice was closed and unused, and Xingwen sluice was built; moreover Xinzhuang and other sluices were repaired, Qingjiangpu's southern dike was built, and Ban sluice's grain dike was newly created, joining north and south with new and old dikes.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Guifang and Shao Yuanzhe also extended Shanyang's long dike seventy li from Ban sluice to Huangpu; Tongji sluice was closed and Xingwen sluice built instead; Xinzhuang and other sluices were repaired, Qingjiangpu's southern dike was raised, and a new grain dike was built at Ban sluice, linking north and south with the old and new embankments.

sentences.zh: 板閘即故移風閘也。

translations.literal: Ban sluice is the former Yifeng sluice.
translations.idiomatic: Ban sluice was the old Yifeng sluice.

sentences.zh: 堤、閘並修，淮、揚漕道漸固。

translations.literal: With dikes and sluices repaired together, the Huai-Yang grain route gradually grew firm.
translations.idiomatic: With dikes and sluices repaired together, the Huai-Yang transport route gradually stabilized.

sentences.zh: 六年，總理河漕都御史潘季馴築高家堰，及清江浦柳浦灣以東加築禮、智二壩，修寶應、黃清等八淺堤，高、寶減水閘四，又拆新莊閘而改建通濟閘於甘羅城南。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Grand Canal Censor-in-Chief Pan Jixun built Gaojiayan, and east of Qingjiangpu's Liupu Bay added the Li and Zhi dams; repaired dikes at eight shallows including Baoying and Huangqing; four flood-discharge sluices at Gaoyou and Baoying; and dismantled Xinzhuang sluice to rebuild Tongji sluice south of Ganluo city.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 6, Grand Canal Censor-in-Chief Pan Jixun built Gaojiayan; east of Qingjiangpu's Liupu Bay he added the Li and Zhi dams; repaired dikes at eight shallows including Baoying and Huangqing; built four flood-discharge sluices in Gaoyou and Baoying; and dismantled Xinzhuang sluice to rebuild Tongji sluice south of Ganluo city.

sentences.zh: 明初運糧，自瓜、儀至淮安謂之裏河，自五壩轉黃河謂之外河，不相通。

translations.literal: In early Ming grain transport, from Guazhou and Yizhen to Huai'an was called the inner river; from the Five Dams turning onto the Yellow River was called the outer river—they did not connect.
translations.idiomatic: In early Ming times, transport from Guazhou and Yizhen to Huai'an was called the inner route; from the Five Dams onto the Yellow River was the outer route—and the two did not connect.

sentences.zh: 及開清江浦，設閘天妃口，春夏之交重運畢，即閉以拒黃。

translations.literal: When Qingjiangpu was opened and a sluice set at Tianfei Mouth, at the turn of spring and summer when heavy transport finished, it was closed to repel the Yellow.
translations.idiomatic: When Qingjiangpu was opened and a sluice installed at Tianfei Mouth, the gate was closed after the main grain convoys passed in late spring and early summer to shut out the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 歲久法馳，閘不封而黃水入。

translations.literal: Over years the rule lapsed; the sluice was not sealed and Yellow water entered.
translations.idiomatic: Over time the rule lapsed, the sluice was left open, and Yellow River water poured in.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖末，塞天妃口，於浦南三里溝開新河，設通濟閘以就淮水。

translations.literal: At the end of Jiajing, Tianfei Mouth was blocked; south of the pu at Sanligou a new river was opened and Tongji sluice set to reach Huai water.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jiajing reign, Tianfei Mouth was blocked; a new channel was cut at Sanligou south of the pu, and Tongji sluice was built to draw on Huai water.

sentences.zh: 已又從萬恭言，復天妃閘。

translations.literal: Soon after, following Wan Gong's words, Tianfei sluice was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, following Wan Gong's advice, Tianfei sluice was restored.

sentences.zh: 未幾又從御史劉光國言，增築通濟，自仲夏至季秋，隔日一放回空漕船。

translations.literal: Before long, following Censor Liu Guangguo's words, Tongji was extended; from midsummer to late autumn, empty return grain boats were released every other day.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, following Censor Liu Guangguo's proposal, Tongji sluice was expanded; from midsummer to late autumn, empty return grain boats were released every other day.

sentences.zh: 既而啟閉不時，淤塞日甚，開硃家口引清水灌之，僅通舟。

translations.literal: Soon opening and closing were untimely, silting grew daily worse; Zhujiakou was opened to lead clear water to flush it—boats barely passed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the sluice was opened and closed at the wrong times, silting worsened by the day; Zhujiakou was opened to flush it with clear water, and boats barely got through.

sentences.zh: 至是改建甘羅城南，專向淮水，使河不得直射。

translations.literal: At this point it was rebuilt south of Ganluo city, facing Huai water exclusively, so the river could not strike straight in.
translations.idiomatic: It was then rebuilt south of Ganluo city to draw solely on Huai water, so the channel would not take the river's full force head-on.

sentences.zh: 十年，督漕尚書淩雲翼以運船由清江浦出口多艱險，乃自浦西開永濟河四十五里，起城南窯灣，曆龍江閘，至楊家澗出武家墩，折而東，合通濟閘出口。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Grain Transport Minister Ling Yunyi, because transport boats leaving Qingjiangpu faced many hardships and dangers, opened Yongji River forty-five li west of the pu—from Yaowan south of the city, passing Longjiang sluice, to Yangjiajian exiting at Wujiadun, turning east to join Tongji sluice's outlet.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 10, Grain Transport Minister Ling Yunyi, finding the Qingjiangpu outlet too hazardous for grain boats, cut the Yongji River forty-five li west of the pu—from Yaowan south of the city, through Longjiang sluice, to Yangjiajian and out at Wujiadun, then east to join the Tongji sluice outlet.

sentences.zh: 更置閘三，以備清江浦之險。

translations.literal: Three more sluices were placed to guard against Qingjiangpu's dangers.
translations.idiomatic: Three additional sluices were installed to bypass Qingjiangpu's hazards.

sentences.zh: 是時漕河就治，淮、揚免水災者十餘年。

translations.literal: At this time the grain canal was brought to order; Huai and Yang were free of flood disaster for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: By then the canal had been brought under control, and Huai and Yang went more than ten years without flood disaster.

sentences.zh: 初，黃河之害漕也，自金龍口而東，則會通以淤。

translations.literal: At first, when the Yellow River harmed transport, from Jinlong Mouth eastward the Huitong section silted.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when the Yellow River threatened transport, the harm lay east of Jinlong Mouth, where the Huitong section silted up.

sentences.zh: 迨塞沙灣、張秋閘，漕以安，則徐、沛間數被其害。

translations.literal: When Shawan and Zhangqiu sluice were blocked and transport was secure, then between Xu and Pei disaster struck repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: After Shawan and Zhangqiu sluice were blocked and transport was secure, the Xu-Pei region suffered repeatedly instead.

sentences.zh: 至崔鎮高堰之決，黃、淮交漲而害漕，乃在淮、揚間，湖潰則敗漕。

translations.literal: When Cuizhen and Gaojiayan breached, Yellow and Huai rose together and harmed transport—the harm lay between Huai and Yang; when lakes burst, transport failed.
translations.idiomatic: After the breaches at Cuizhen and Gaojiayan, when the Yellow and Huai rose together and threatened transport, the danger shifted to the Huai-Yang region—when the lakes broke, transport failed.

sentences.zh: 季馴以高堰障洪澤，俾堰東四湖勿受淮侵，漕始無敗。

translations.literal: Jixun used Gaojiayan to block Hongze, causing the four lakes east of the weir not to suffer Huai invasion—only then did transport cease to fail.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Jixun used Gaojiayan to hold back Hongze Lake, keeping the four lakes east of the weir from Huai flooding—only then did transport stop failing.

sentences.zh: 而河漕諸臣懼湖害，日夜常惴惴。

translations.literal: Yet the canal officials feared lake harm and were constantly anxious day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the canal officials, fearing what the lakes might do, lived in constant dread.

sentences.zh: 十三年從總漕都御史李世達議，開寶應月河。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, following the proposal of Li Shida, Censor-in-Chief for Grain Transport, they opened the Baoying relief canal.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, following Grand Coordinator for Grain Transport Li Shida's proposal, the Baoying relief canal was opened.

sentences.zh: 寶應汜光湖，諸湖中最湍險者也，廣百二十餘里。

translations.literal: Baoying's Siguang Lake was the most turbulent and treacherous of all the lakes, more than a hundred and twenty li across.
translations.idiomatic: Baoying's Siguang Lake was the roughest and most dangerous of all the lakes, spanning more than a hundred and twenty li.

sentences.zh: 槐角樓當其中，形曲如箕，瓦店翼其南，秤鉤灣翼其北。

translations.literal: Huaijiao Tower stood at its center, curving like a winnowing basket; Wadian flanked its south, Chenggou Bay its north.
translations.idiomatic: Huaijiao Tower lay at its center in a curve shaped like a winnowing tray, with Wadian on its south flank and Chenggou Bay on its north.

sentences.zh: 西風鼓浪，往往覆舟。

translations.literal: West winds stirred waves, and boats often capsized.
translations.idiomatic: When west winds whipped up the waves, boats capsized with alarming frequency.

sentences.zh: 陳瑄築堤湖東，蓄水為運道。

translations.literal: Chen Xuan built dikes on the lake's east side, storing water to serve as the transport channel.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xuan built dikes along the lake's eastern shore, impounding water to create a transport channel.

sentences.zh: 上有所受，下無所宣，遂決為八淺，匯為六潭，興、鹽諸場皆沒。

translations.literal: Above there was intake but below no outlet; it burst into eight shallows and pooled into six ponds, and the Xing and Yan salt works were all submerged.
translations.idiomatic: Water had somewhere to enter above but nowhere to discharge below; the lake broke into eight shallows and six pools, inundating the salt fields of Xing and Yan.

sentences.zh: 而淮水又從周家橋漫入，溺人民，害漕運。

translations.literal: Moreover, Huai waters also flooded in through Zhoujia Bridge, drowning people and harming grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: Huai River water also poured in through Zhoujia Bridge, drowning people and disrupting the grain transport route.

sentences.zh: 武宗末年，郎中楊最請開月河，部覆不從。

translations.literal: In the final years of Emperor Wuzong, Director Yang Zui requested opening a relief canal; the ministry memorialized in reply and did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: In the last years of the Wuzong reign, Director Yang Zui petitioned to open a relief canal, but the ministry's reply rejected the proposal.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，工部郎中陳毓賢、戶部員外範韶、御史聞人詮、運糧千戶李顯皆以為言，議行未果。

translations.literal: During the Jiajing reign, Works Director Chen Yuxian, Revenue Vice Director Fan Shao, Censor Wen Renquan, and Grain Transport Company Commander Li Xian all spoke on the matter, but deliberation did not result in action.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiajing period, Chen Yuxian of the Ministry of Works, Fan Shao of the Ministry of Revenue, Censor Wen Renquan, and grain transport commander Li Xian all urged the same course, yet the plan was never carried out.

sentences.zh: 至是，工部郎中許應逵建議，世達用其言以奏，乃決行之。

translations.literal: At this time, Works Director Xu Yingkui made a proposal; Li Shida adopted his words in a memorial, and the decision was made to proceed.
translations.idiomatic: Now Xu Yingkui, a director in the Ministry of Works, submitted a plan; Li Shida endorsed it in a memorial to the throne, and the project was finally approved.

sentences.zh: 浚河千七百餘丈，置石閘三，減水閘二，築堤九千餘丈，石堤三之一，子堤五千餘丈。

translations.literal: They dredged the canal more than one thousand seven hundred zhang, installed three stone locks and two flood gates, built dikes more than nine thousand zhang long—one third of them stone—and subsidiary dikes more than five thousand zhang.
translations.idiomatic: More than seventeen hundred zhang of canal were dredged; three stone locks and two flood gates were installed; dikes totaling over nine thousand zhang were raised, a third of them faced in stone, along with more than five thousand zhang of secondary dikes.

sentences.zh: 工成，賜名弘濟。

translations.literal: When the work was completed, it was granted the name Hongji.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished, the canal received the imperial name Hongji, "Great Relief."

sentences.zh: 尋改石閘為平水閘。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the stone locks were converted to level-water gates.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the stone locks were rebuilt as level-water gates.

sentences.zh: 應逵又築高郵護城堤。

translations.literal: Xu Yingkui also built Gaoyou's city-protection dike.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yingkui also constructed the protective dike around Gaoyou city.

sentences.zh: 其後，弘濟南北閘，夏秋淮漲，吞吐不及，舟多覆者。

translations.literal: Afterward, at Hongji's north and south gates, when the Huai rose in summer and autumn the gates could not take in and release water fast enough, and many boats capsized.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at the north and south locks of Hongji, summer and autumn Huai floods overwhelmed the gates' capacity, and many transport boats were lost.

sentences.zh: 神宗季年，督漕侍郎陳薦於南北各開月河以殺河怒，而溜始平。

translations.literal: In the late years of Emperor Shenzong, Grain Transport Vice Minister Chen Jian opened relief canals on both north and south to dissipate the river's fury, and the currents gradually settled.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Wanli reign, Vice Minister Chen Jian, supervising grain transport, opened relief canals on both the north and south sides to tame the river's force, and the currents at last grew calm.

sentences.zh: 十五年，督漕侍郎楊一魁請修高家堰以保上流，砌範家口以制旁決，疏草灣以殺河勢，修禮壩以保新城。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, Grain Transport Vice Minister Yang Yikui requested repairing Gaojiayan to protect the upper reaches, building up Fanjiakou to control lateral breaches, dredging Caowan to reduce river force, and repairing Liba to protect Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, Vice Minister Yang Yikui petitioned to repair Gaojiayan to secure the upper stream, block Fanjiakou against side breaches, dredge Caowan to break the river's momentum, and restore Liba to protect Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 詔如其議。

translations.literal: An edict approved as he proposed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered that his proposal be carried out.

sentences.zh: 一魁又改建古洪閘。

translations.literal: Yang Yikui also rebuilt Guhong Lock.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yikui also reconstructed Guhong Lock.

sentences.zh: 先是，汶、泗之水由茶城會黃河。

translations.literal: Previously, the waters of the Wen and Si joined the Yellow River at Chacheng.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Wen and Si rivers had met the Yellow River at Chacheng.

sentences.zh: 隆慶間，濁流倒灌，稽阻運船，郎中陳瑛移黃河口於茶城東八里，建古洪、內華二閘，漕河從古洪出口。

translations.literal: During the Longqing reign, turbid backflow obstructed transport boats; Director Chen Ying moved the Yellow River mouth eight li east of Chacheng, built Guhong and Neihua locks, and the canal exited through Guhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the Longqing period, muddy backflow blocked transport vessels; Director Chen Ying relocated the Yellow River mouth eight li east of Chacheng, built the Guhong and Neihua locks, and routed the canal out through Guhong.

sentences.zh: 後黃水發，淤益甚。

translations.literal: Later, when Yellow River waters rose, silting grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: Later, whenever the Yellow River swelled, silting grew steadily worse.

sentences.zh: 一魁既改古洪，帝又從給事中常居敬言，令增築鎮口閘於古洪外，距河僅八十丈，吐納益易，糧運利之。

translations.literal: After Yang Yikui had rebuilt Guhong, the emperor also followed Supervising Censor Chang Jujing's words, ordering Zhenkou Lock built outside Guhong, only eighty zhang from the river, making intake and discharge easier and benefiting grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yang Yikui had rebuilt Guhong, the emperor also accepted Supervising Censor Chang Jujing's advice and ordered Zhenkou Lock added beyond Guhong, a mere eighty zhang from the river, so that water could enter and leave more easily and grain transport profited.

sentences.zh: 工部尚書石星議季馴、居敬條上善後事宜，請分地責成：接築塔山縷堤，清江浦草壩，創築寶應西堤，石砌邵伯湖堤，疏浚裏河淤淺，當在淮、揚興舉；

translations.literal: Minister of Works Shi Xing reviewed the follow-up measures listed by Ji Xun and Chang Jujing, requesting division of responsibility by region: continuing Tashan thread-dike, Qingjiangpu grass dam, new Baoying west dike, stone Shaobo Lake dike, and dredging the silted inner canal—these should be undertaken in Huai and Yang;
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Shi Xing reviewed the follow-up proposals submitted by Ji Xun and Chang Jujing and called for assigning tasks by region: extending the Tashan thread-dike, the Qingjiangpu grass dam, a new Baoying west dike, stone facing for the Shaobo Lake dike, and dredging the silted inner canal—all to be undertaken in the Huai-Yang area;

sentences.zh: 察復南旺、馬踏、蜀山、馬場四湖，建築坎河滾水壩，加建通濟、永通二閘，察復安山湖地，當在山東興舉。

translations.literal: investigating restoration of the four lakes Nanwang, Mata, Shushan, and Machang, building Kanhe overflow dams, adding Tongji and Yongtong locks, and investigating restoration of Anshan Lake lands—these should be undertaken in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: restoring the four lakes of Nanwang, Mata, Shushan, and Machang, building Kanhe overflow dams, adding the Tongji and Yongtong locks, and reclaiming the lands of Anshan Lake—all to be undertaken in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 帝從其議。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted the plan.

sentences.zh: 未幾，眾工皆成。

translations.literal: Before long, all the projects were completed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, every project was finished.

sentences.zh: 十九年，季馴言：「宿遷以南，地形西ＡＨ，請開縷堤放水。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, Ji Xun said: "South of Suqian, the terrain slopes high to the west; I request opening a thread-dike to release water.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, Pan Jixun reported: "South of Suqian the land rises toward the west; I propose opening a thread-dike to release water.

sentences.zh: 沙隨水入，地隨沙高，庶水患消而費可省。」

translations.literal: Sand will enter with the water, and the land will rise with the sand; perhaps water disasters will abate and expense can be saved."
translations.idiomatic: Sand would come in with the water and raise the ground level, so that flood damage might ease and costs be reduced."

sentences.zh: 又請易高家堰土堤為石，築滿家閘西攔河壩，使汶、泗盡歸新河。

translations.literal: He also requested converting Gaojiayan's earthen dike to stone, building a river-blocking dam west of Manjia Lock, and causing all Wen and Si waters to flow into the new canal.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to replace Gaojiayan's earthen dike with stone, build a river-blocking dam west of Manjia Lock, and divert all Wen and Si waters into the new canal.

sentences.zh: 設減水閘於李家口，以泄沛縣積水。

translations.literal: He proposed flood gates at Lijiakou to drain Pei County's accumulated water.
translations.idiomatic: Flood gates were to be installed at Lijiakou to discharge Pei County's pooled water.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 十月，淮湖大漲，江都淳家灣石堤、邵伯南壩、高郵中堤、硃家墩、清水潭皆決。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, the Huai lakes rose greatly; the stone dike at Chunjiawan in Jiangdu, Shaobo's south dam, Gaoyou's middle dike, Zhujiadun, and Qingshuitan all breached.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the Huai lakes surged; the stone dike at Chunjiawan in Jiangdu, the south dam at Shaobo, Gaoyou's middle dike, Zhujiadun, and Qingshuitan all gave way.

sentences.zh: 郎中黃日謹築塞僅竣，而山陽堤亦決。

translations.literal: Director Huang Rijin had barely finished building and sealing the breaches when the Shanyang dike also broke.
translations.idiomatic: Director Huang Rijin had scarcely finished the repairs when the Shanyang dike breached as well.

sentences.zh: 二十一年五月，恆雨。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the twenty-first year, rain fell continuously.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the twenty-first year, unending rain fell.

sentences.zh: 漕河泛溢，潰濟甯及淮河諸堤岸。

translations.literal: The canal overflowed, bursting the dikes and banks of Jining and the Huai River.
translations.idiomatic: The canal burst its banks, destroying the dikes along Jining and the Huai River.

sentences.zh: 總河尚書舒應龍議：築堽城壩，遏汶水之南，開馬踏湖月河口，導汶水之北。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator for Rivers Shu Yinglong proposed: build Qiangcheng dam to block Wen water to the south, open Mata Lake's relief canal mouth, and guide Wen water to the north.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Shu Yinglong proposed building Qiangcheng dam to hold Wen water on the south, opening Mata Lake's relief canal mouth, and directing Wen water northward.

sentences.zh: 開通濟閘，放月河土壩以殺洶湧之勢。
